title: Bears-Titans game preview, joint practice recap | Bears Weekly
text: Welcome [music] in to Bears Weekly, a Chicago Bears Network production. Bears Weekly [music] is brought to you by Advocate Healthcare, Atletico Physical Therapy, CDW, Conniey's Pizza, and Menor Light. Here are your hosts, Jeff Jiac, aka the mayor of Bearsville, [music] and his sidekick, Tom the Surf Master. From [music] a warm and humid Nashville, Tennessee, we enjoyed a hard-fought practice between the Bears and Titans leading to Saturday [music] night's preseason finale at 5:00 right here on ESPN 1000 of the Bears Radio Network at Nissan Stadium. We discuss tonight on Bears Weekly on ESPN 1000 with Super Bowl winning Bears guard Tom the I'm Jeff Jonia. Thanks to Dan Burelli, Jordan Treup, Katie Fox, our producer Kendra Smith tonight, and the executive producer of the Bears radio and Eric Eric Estroski. Coming up in tonight's program, we hear from head coach Ben Johnson from this morning's media chat. That was before practice. A check-in with Bears veteran special team ace and defensive end Daniel Hardy and a postpractice sound from Caleb Williams and defensive tackle Grady Jarrett. Tom, learned a lot today. First of all, nice facility the Titans have here down in Nashville. But it was football nirvana. We're between two fields watching the Bears defense against the number ones offensively of the Titans, number one defense of the Titans, and the number one Bears offense right between the fields gauging uh plays cuz there it was like a 28 play team episode there at the end. It was awesome. >> You know, hot enough to get you sweaty, but hot enough to get you in shape. It was perfect conditions out there. The field conditions are absolutely perfect and I think it was a super worthy practice. Both teams got a lot of out of it. Both teams had a physical approach. I think Ben Johnson and Robert Salah are both two good head coaches that, you know, get the most out of their football team. So, a lot of good things went on today and I think the Bears benefited from it. >> Yeah. Early great red zone again uh for Caleb Williams. He was hot early. He hit eight different receivers at one point as I was checking boxes on guys. There was some playful uh Ben Johnson type trick plays. Also, a lot of heated battles throughout the day. Uh that that defense of of um Tennessee play some physicality to it. So, you kind of got a little bit out of everything from it. I heard also Robert Salah saying, "Hey, you get a heck of a lot more out of these joint practices than you do a game." >> You really do because you can dictate and decide everything. You can script every period and every play. You can ask for the defenses you want to see and you can ask for the plays that you need to be challenged by and then you get an opportunity to have repeated efforts on certain special team plays where it's not just a punt in a game. Then you go on to a series. You may have 10 punts in the in the course of a practice or extra point and field goals. There's just a lot of elements to these practices that can be scripted which I think benefit the teams. All right, here's head coach Ben Johnson before practice and why two weeks in a row on the road kind of a plan for the head coach. >> We knew that we wanted a week two and a week three joint practice. We thought that was the best way to get our team prepared for not just week one but the first four games of the season. Uh and we're executing that plan right now. We we assess it every single day. Brent Salazar part of our staff meetings at night. He always is hitting us with who the workload, who's got the heavy volume, the the high uh high speed yardage, the A cells, D cell. He's got all that that uh mumbo jumbo, if you will, and and we try our best as coaches just to make sure we're we're taking care of our guys. >> Did Austin Booker get banged up in that practice last week in Cincinnati? And what's his status right now? >> Yeah, he he's he's banged up. Um he's working through a groin and and it'll be more week to week in terms of his availability. >> Would you bring Marcus Davenport? Uh, has he been dealing with something as well? >> He's not dealing with anything. He's, uh, we want to make sure we're being smart with him. He's a player that's missed a lot of time over the last three years. And so, uh, he's being integrated into the program from conditioning to strength program, uh, drill work and and we're slowly ramping him into it. >> And [music] did Dexter come down here with you? >> Dexter's not here. >> Okay. What happened to him if you saw him come off the other? >> Yeah, he's got a hamstring. [music] >> Been very positive about DeAndre and the camp he's having. Where have you seen his progress in understanding the concepts and the tracks that you're looking for? >> Yeah. No, I think he and I just had the conversation the other day. It's it's the best I've seen him this time of year and uh you look back at a year ago, he was very explosive and yet it takes a little while to gel between him, the offensive line. I think he's he's accelerating his vision here at this point. I think coach Studesville has been fantastic for him um just with the reads and being able to know the intent of where we're trying to hit things. Um he bounces it when we're supposed to bounce it. He hits it right on the spot when it's there and then he cuts it up. I think he's doing a doing a really good job right now. Um got we just got to get him to that first week nice and healthy and and ready to go. I think he's prime for a big year though. >> Back weeks you see Dexter Lawrence and now Jeffree kind of two different players but >> you might not see many better defensive tackles all regular season. No slight against >> No, I I think this was this was by design. We want to challenge our offensive line and uh you know certainly it's great work for Jonah and Joe, but we'll get Newman in there a little bit, Jordan McFaden in there a little bit and see see where they're at as well in their development. Completely different style of defense this week than what we just saw. This is an attacking front that they they want to meet us on our side of the line of scrimmage and knock us back. Um and it's not just Jeffrey Simmons. He is the the bellcow from what I can understand, but they they've upgraded um you know Frank the Meyers from from Denver. He's got he had a really good year last year. Germaine Johnson they traded for from the Jets. Uh and so it's going to be all around a big test for us up front. A little bit different style than what we've seen so far. >> With Dylan at safety, how would you characterize maybe the growth development you're seeing? >> He I had just joked around with the team a couple days ago just I I don't even know what his voice sounds like really. He just he just comes into work and and gets after it. Um little bit robotic like that in a good way. I'm I'm saying that as a compliment. he just puts his head down and grinds. And what you've seen is slow and steady progress throughout. You've seen some of the ball production uh last week, certainly in Cincinnati, uh getting the interception. That was one of the best plays of that practice. Uh and what you're seeing now is him really honing in on taking good angles, whether he's the quarter safety, post safety, down safety, really doesn't matter where he's aligning, making sure he's taking good angles and stopping the football that way. So, really pleased with where he's at as well. Where's Rous at right now in terms of being ready to handle at least that >> he's building that trust? Um there's flashes where gets you really really excited. Is it at the level of consistency that we want yet? No. The answer is no. And uh and I'm not surprised by that either yet. I think he's going to be a phenomenal football player for a long time in this league. It's just there's a lot of thinking. There's a lot on the plate for a for a rookie tight end. Um, I think it's right up there with quarterback just in terms of the the amount of mental that strain that we put on these guys, run game, uh, pass pro, run, route running, and the faster we can get him to play, the better off he's going to be in the long run. But it's it's by design very challenging for him right now. And I know Coach Dre, uh, Robbie Picazo's in that room, myself, like we're very hard on him and he's answering that call. Ben, one of the questions that always seems to irritate you is anything that's premised on last year. Uh, why does that annoy you? And what are some ways that you're specifically coaching this team differently? >> Are you trying to annoy me right now? [laughter] >> Yeah. Um, listen, all I care about is does it help us win or not? That's that's really what what I'm all about. Like we can talk about injuries up here. The guys that aren't out there, they're not helping us win right now. I want to talk about the guys that are out there helping us right now. I want I want stories to be written about those guys. They just we got 90 guys on the roster right now, a lot of which are fighting for their their professional lives right now and uh their stories are incredible. They should be out there and and and hearing about that. But talking about last year isn't going to do us any good in terms of winning this practice, winning the next preseason game, winning week one. And that's really all we care about right now. >> Ben Johnson, many topics, injuries, uh but the end is the best. uh does it help us win? And and that's where he's been since he got here. And so any answers to questions about a year ago or whatever. Yeah. He he doesn't he's not a 50,000 foot view guy. He wants to know about him right now. He want he wants he wants to be ground level, >> right? He wants to talk about things that are relevant. He wants the things that want to talk about that are relevant to the improvement of this football team. And he doesn't have time to waste on, you know, hypotheticals or questions about the past. So, you know, I'm glad he's upfront with these guys about that type of uh questioning and, you know, ask me something that's pertinent to tomorrow. >> All right. Well, tomorrow is today and we get ready for Caleb Williams and his news conference after practice on this day here on Bears Weekly on ESPN 1000 and the Bears radio network. >> [music] >> Welcome back to Bears Weekly, a Chicago Bears production on the flagship home of the Bears, ESPN [music] Chicago. This [music] segment of Bears Weekly is brought to you by Athletico Physical Therapy. Visit athletico.com to request [music] an in clinic or virtual appointment and start feeling better tomorrow. Here with Tom the Jeff Jonia as the Bears wrapped up their practice session with the Tennessee Titans. Effectively timed the last practice of training camp. there's a week week zero when they get back before they start getting ready for week one. >> Yeah. You know, listen, they have a lot in the rearview mirror. They've been able to improve in a lot of areas and they've been trying to make some tough decisions going forward. So, whatever they did on the practice field against the Cincinnati Bengals and Tennessee Titans, that's behind them. It's going to be interesting for the guys that are in anticipating an opportunity to play against the Tennessee Titans because this is the unfortunate and the life side of it. This is the last time some of these guys will ever put on football equipment and you don't want that to be you including in that conversation. So go out there and dress to impress and that's what you got to try to do on the n on this stage on Saturday night. Tyson Ber did a nice job. Had some great bucket in the bucket throws to players. Uh went to make a tackle after an interception and would not let the guy score. That that raised a ruckus on the Tennessee sideline. Jeffrey Simmons leading the charge. But that kind of that play in my opinion kind of set the tone for the rest of practice because you had everybody from Luther Burton uh chewing the ear of uh that that defense over there to Jade A Walker to the other side of the field of course uh where there was a big play. You'll probably see highlights of it, but uh Xavier Woods, the veteran safety added to the Bears, he u there was a throw over the middle. Wandelle Robinson, the former New York Giant took took the worst of that one and flee concussion for Robinson. But it is the way the the Bears want to bring a tone. >> Well, Xavier Woods in terms of that in the instantaneousness of that hit, you cannot stop your body midstride. So, was it cheap? Nah. You know, that's, you know, that's a topic for people to talk about, but I it's just the way that the speed that football works at and Xavier Woods does not have time to slow down, stop or hesitate. >> Robert Sal in his news conference also said he's a huge fan of Caleb Williams. Uh told Ben Johnson, you know what, teams better be up three scores in the fourth quarter in order to keep him from coming from behind. Uh said that the amount of growth over the last 18 months of Caleb Williams has been amazing. Uh he's a stud in every way. So we got the up close personal look at him. Doesn't have to throw bouquets. He's not playing them in the season. So >> yeah, but that sure is some nice compliments from a defensive coordinator, head coach u that you know has sent probably seen very little of Caleb in actual studied film. >> There's Caleb Williams from practice earlier today, >> last week to to this week is just working on execution, um the flags and things like that. Um, and then and then also like uh I said, it's it's it's leading uh from the head of the snake down to the tail. And you know, when we come out with good energy when we come out and we're executing, when we come out, we're not having penalties and things like that as as first team. Um, it trickles down, um, you know, to second team and third team. And just having that energy and so, uh, being able to start like that, we got to we got to be able to start like that throughout the year. And then, uh, you know, when we when we come out from halftime, we got to come out better, I would say, than we did today. Was it to Swift on the toss back to you for the throw? >> Oh, it was a pretty good toss, too. Uh yeah. Yeah, Swift uh threw it back to me. It was a double pass. Swift threw it back to me. Um tight end Coloulston and and Rome did a good job. I believe it was Rome over there on the left side of X. Uh he did a good job uh just just being really patient, letting the, you know, letting the play develop and happen and then just shooting down the field, taking the deep coverage out and Coulson lost his guy, so it was it was really cool. >> Did they say anything about a a trick play in practice? >> Uh who, the Titans? Uh, no. If they did, I didn't hear them. Yeah. >> How did you feel about the red zone work overall? >> Um, how much red zone work did we get today? >> Early. >> It wasn't It wasn't much. Uh, felt solid. I I think uh was that seven on? I'm I'm I'm blanking on on on the day. Sorry. Um, seven on. I I missed the pass that I should have hit early on, the first first or second pass, and then I think I only had three reps or so. And so, I think the other two we hit. So, um, obviously you want to go three for three. I would say seven on especially is is is a offensive advantage play, uh, or or situation. And so, uh, just trying to be as consistent as possible. >> Reload's been pretty good. Yep. >> Um, where do you feel like you've gotten better at processing? >> Yeah. Uh, I wouldn't say it's processing. I think it's just I think it's just understanding the play better of the plays that that we put in. Um, and then not having to necessarily, you know, relearn plays and things like that or or or you know, just learn plays overall. Um, and and coach can add in more detail. Coach can add in more uh more plays and and so um it's been fun. It's been exciting. And then, uh, you know, just just my feet, I would say, has been the biggest thing down there. Just being able to be in in rhythm and and smooth and delivering the guys a good ball. >> Do you have confidence in the low tackle situation right now? Yeah, I uh I didn't I mean other than that one period where it wasn't just the left tackle, we had guys coming, you know, down the middle, the right side, left side. And so um you know, I I feel good. I've played with both those guys out there um between Braxton and and Theo. And so we got live reps, we got real reps, we got game reps, we got practice reps over the past, I guess I mean it's three years now for me um going into my third year. And so, um, yeah, I feel I feel good with with, uh, where those guys are at and whatever co, uh, decision coach makes. >> Ben's been pushing recently for the next jump from you in recognition. How do you describe what is next for you in that? >> Yeah, it's just, >> you know, at times you have you have five guys going out in a in a um in a in a concept. And so portions of the concepts are specific for certain uh certain coverages or certain looks. And so, uh, just just not necessarily going one, two, three, four, five. It's it's okay, we can we can skip this route because of this coverage or you know this post high or you know they're split split field and and things like that. And so um you know it's just being able to process those things faster. And it's it's just been like I said like I said it's it's just been faster or or or more comfortable with the plays and being able to uh not necessarily think about the plays anymore. You know I'm I'm I'm more or less getting up there and trying to figure out uh you know what I can fix uh to make sure this play works or make sure this you know this um this drive works. And so, um, you know, and there's times where we may have the coverage and something happens and it's being able to adjust and find a check down, a scramble, and and and be positive in in those ways. >> How do you learn to process now, guys? Is it just as simple as reps? >> Oh, man. It's reps. It's reps. And it's not just it's not on the grass and between the 120 and 53. It's it's being able to consistently I mean, I write the same like if it's um a common concept, you know, that that everybody runs in. I write it down consistently. I write down the uh you know what we like it verse, what we don't like at verse. Um every time the play is put in and installed and so it's just I'm getting constant mental reps of of you know when I see a coverage or when I see this it's it's okay we don't like it versus this. Now let's get on to the the back side of the concept or you know another route that you know uh that we that we do like in that concept. All right, Caleb Williams, I I want you to tell me what you're hearing about the growth of Caleb Williams from that those answers he didn't give two years ago or even a year ago. >> Um, a super confident mind that's developing an association with Ben Johnson that can be creatively put to use in practice and have a lot of carryover to the game. And whether it's the installation of a trick play just to show the audience you might never use it, but they always know you got it. And then he makes a reference to the the 120 53. You know what he's talking about there. >> Yes. >> And but a lot of people don't. The dimensions of a football field and it's really one it's 53 and a third. but he makes references to instances in time that he is so familiar with that he can repeat and recall a lot of practice information from the from the past that is going to factor into his future. So, I'm excited to see where that's going. >> Also, he touched on things like leadership. You know, he he still feels in his world that uh the best teams are led by the locker room. And so Ben's pushing that, pushing him, pushing others on this team to make sure that that happens because there was a we talked about a leadership void. When a guy like um you know leaves the team and has been here for a while, that's a leadership void. You got to find new leaders. They have to come organically. Uh but he also said, you know, Ben wants them to be excited when they score. So you often see Caleb not in the play, running down the field when something big happens. and he made reference to Tony Parker and San Antonio during their heyday, the Spurs, that they would high-five each other more than any other team in the league. It's just that excitement of the payoff. Well, let me say something about that leadership role because last year we talked about that there was no captains from the offense and defensive line. So, you can still be a leader, but you're not a captain. So don't see the anointment of the captains here within the next couple weeks and say, "Oh my god, if this guy's not on it, he's must not be a leader." That's not the case at all. Every there's a lot of guys in that locker room that are leaders that just you don't hear from them very often. It's like the interview that we're going to hear with Daniel Hardy. I'm super excited that you have this interview cuz people need exposure to this young guy. >> Coming up next, Grady Jarrett out of ESPN 1000 on the Bears Radio Network. Jeff Jonia [music] and Tom the chatting about the Bears. It must be Bears Weekly. >> Well, if it's Bears Weekly, >> it must be the home of the Bears. [music] ESPN Chicago. Jeff and Tom back with you on ESPN 1000, the Bears Radio Network. We're brought to you by Athletico Physical Therapy. Visit athletico.com to request an in clinic or virtual appointment and start feeling better tomorrow. Grady Jarrett, a senior member of that defensive line with a lot of lot of different veterans on there. an area where Ben Johnson continues to express his confidence in at defensive tackle, meeting with the media after practice and the overall tone of what this practice was. >> Can't finish training camp without a good burner. So, today we had one. It was fun to come out here and compete against them, man. It was awesome day. So, uh feel good and excited to, you know, um get to the end of the preseason and get ready into the um what we got to finish our game obviously and um you know, just continue to build. What do you feel like you've squeezed out of these two joint practices the last two weeks? >> Uh I think just seeing where we at as a team uh being able to compete against uh other other people is always fun and uh we don't have to beat up beat up on each other all the time. So to go against, you know, two teams the last two weeks that's that's really well, really physical. I think we did a really good job and it was good to get to work and we definitely appreciate it. >> Behavior had a pretty big hit in practice early. How do you balance that physicality but also like >> you know uh some we we practice a certain way. um we got, you know, the way we want to play ball and uh nothing is done with malice, but we got to play our style of defense the way we want to at all times and um and you know, sometimes things happen and I mean, you know, just one of those things that happen, but you know, it is what it kind of is what it is. You know, >> it looked like early on you guys really wanted to set the tempo with that that play style. Was that kind of the messaging going on? >> I mean, I would I would just say every time we take the field, it's the style of defense we want to play. Um and um I think we did that early. I think our key now is to sustain that through the um whole through the whole outing, whether it's the whole game. Feel like at the halftime, you know, we had to reamp it back up, but we got to find a way to continue to challenge ourselves to keep that physical that aggressiveness all the way through the end of the game. And that's how I think we take the next step, but I mean, we we want to play our style of defense anytime we have the opportunity to. And um and I think we I think we did well. Freddy, uh, the coaches talk about the, uh, uh, interior depth being a, uh, a plus this year. Who have you seen make the most of, uh, that opportunity from your unit? >> I think it's been a collective effort. Like I said back in the spring, um, was just getting back to the basics of the style we want to play, the way we want to be in our stands, the way we want to strike off the ball, and I think everybody, it's helping everybody across the board. And um and I just think it's been a collective group effort from the coaches challenges every day, players buying in and uh coming out here executing on the field. And I think everybody reaping the benefits right now uh from the time that we put in in the offseason through training camp and uh we'll continue to as we continue to focus on our fundamentals and try to get better. >> Do you find that Vandenberg just kind of has your ear a lot asking you a lot of questions? Um, I mean, I think it's been an obviously it was, you know, um, that's the part that seen a lot, but it's a lot of work put in with all the guys, man. From the rookies to the vets. We have a really, really healthy um, connection in our room. Um, it worked hand in hand. We talked to the rooks, the rooks talk to us. And, uh, it's been awesome to have that um, just that that that feeling in the room with between the coaches and the players that we can have trust with each other. And we all speak in one language on what's expected. So if he come to me or if I go to somebody else or somebody else go to somebody else, we all speaking the same language. It's just little reminders and um that's that's been a super fun part of this year having a really close-knit group of insiders and and as far as the ends as well. So um we all speaking the same language and that's why we can communicate so well across the board. >> Between the between the heat and and how deep into training camp you guys are now, is this the most intense practice you guys have had? >> I mean I don't know if I'll say most intense. I think it was just the next practice up. You know, at the end of the day, any anybody, anywhere, anytime, we got to do what we do. The job got to get done. And um and uh I don't even think we looking at it like that. We just want to win each day, do our best, and let the rest take care of itself. Uh you got something? >> Yeah. I just want to know what you thought of having a halftime. I don't know if that's something you've had. I I haven't seen >> I've I've had it in the past before. We don't usually do that in um um the way we practice at at home, but it was good. It was good simulation for um actual game time because you going to come out hot and there's going to be a halftime in the game. You got to be able to maintain that and uh that's a growing lesson for us and um so I mean it is what it is. However they want to do it, we we'll be ready to go. >> You wanted to win the day. Did you feel like you guys won the day? >> I mean I feel like we definitely came out put put put a really put a really good effort forward today. Uh we do got to go and review review the tape, but I think the attack mindset was there and um there's a lot to learn from. I think our finish could be better as a whole unit. Um but that's just was a challenge of what come at training camp at the end of it you know hot challenging day which is no excuse but it's also a growth opportunity for us and um but it definitely was a successful productive day and I'm proud of u the whole team not even the defense not just the defense. >> That's great Jared probably was the hottest day for the Bears. I know that both teams had guys that were cramping up uh at various times. You know better than anybody what that's like. Did you feel the same way? The heat and the halftime thing. Yeah, they did go in for a cooling off. had some water, both went into the locker room. I guess Salah Tommy has practices designed to have a full game plus a quarter. That's what he wants. And he had eight. This was the final one of eight of those types of practice. So essentially, he feels they banked enough reps to have had played eight games already this season. >> Interesting. >> I mean, it's what you get out of the reps. And I think Grady explained it a lot. Is this the best practice? No, it was the next practice up. And Grady's the type of guy that he can lead by example and he can lead vocally. So it was neat to see and it was neat to see that cooling down period. So the Tennessee Titans, they have a box about as big as a semi-tra that is a cooling room. So you go in there and at the width of the semi size cooling box, they have two benches. So you walk in there and you can probably fit in 60 guys and the temperature is extreme. So I went in there and I sat there and I just said, "How long could I take this on the extremely hot kind of a day?" And it would be an immediate refresher. And it's just the new science of >> Did they allow the Bears to do the same? They allowed any of the players to do it. It's It could be used as an emergency case scenario, but a cooler for the players. It was pretty cool. >> Always investigating things. I wonder where you went. You turned around and boom, you were gone like the wind. >> Yeah, I sat in that box for a while and it was really neat. >> All right, that's top there. I'm Jeff Jonia. Coming up, my feature interview with Daniel Hardy. It's coming next here on ESPN 1000 of the Bears Radio Network. >> Welcome back to Bears Weekly on the Bears Radio Network. Jeff Joniac and Tom the He'll be back with me in a moment. But first of all, Daniel Hardy, our guest, I'm laughing because Tom the Every time I mention your name on a game. He goes, "That's your guy. That's your guy." I'm the biggest Daniel Hardy supporter in the National Football League. I I just appreciate everything that you do, how you do it, how you've gone about it. You're a true pro man. So, congrats on everything. Uh, and a new two-year deal in the off season. That's huge. So, I really don't even think of it as being a leader. I'm doing my job to the best of my ability and trying to bring other people along and have them do do the same things. >> Do you get asked a lot of questions now that you you're a vet? >> Yeah. Yeah. Um especially, you know, the rookies, the guys coming in um just trying to show them the ropes, how we do things is and the standard that we have around here and trying to uphold that and um you know, just being excellent every day. >> Can you compare camps last year to this? Similar, harder. This year's definitely harder. Um I think >> Tell me why. >> To be honest, we we we got a taste. We we we [laughter] we got a taste. Um you know, after having, you know, poor seasons and then finally experiencing winning and understanding what it took to win and everything that we did last year, it was a lot, but we saw how far it got us and where it got us. And now it's kind of like, you know, when you when you hit on on that table and now you want to go back for more. So now we have to put more in to get more out. >> I thought it was interesting today's practice Jaylen Johnson pulled everybody together. Uh why did he do that? What was said? Um, you know, and that's the again speaking to the kind of the difference between last year and this year is like we understand what it takes to win and the way we started practice was unacceptable and you know Jaylen Johnson being a veteran uh being one of the better guys on this team you know didn't like it called us up and said this practice needs to be we need to take up the intensity up the execution um up the competition. It was, you know, we know the standard now. We know what it takes and we are no longer allowing ourselves to fall below that. >> Daniel Hardy, our guest here on ESPN 1000 of the Bears radio network, getting ready to trip out to Nashville backto back 4day stays basically. title: Matt LaFleur 1-on-1: 'I think my parents wanted a tie tonight'
text: Matt, that was the most entertaining preseason game I've ever seen. How'd you feel about it? >> The same way. That was it was I'm so proud of our guys the way we finished the game. Just battled and made plays in every phase of the game. >> Let's talk about some of the guys that made it so exciting beginning with Kyle McCord. Four touchdown passes, a QB rating of 119 plus. Quite a night. >> Yeah, he had a great night and he got a lot of help from the wide receivers, tight ends. I thought the O-line did a really nice job blocking. Yeah, it was it was a fun night. >> Want to talk about a couple of those wide receivers. Will Shepherd, touchdown catch and a punt return. Like an 81-yard punt return. Jay Michael Sturdivant, TD catch and over 100 yards receiving. They certainly stated their cases. >> Yeah, absolutely. I think they made it really hard on us which is at the end of the day what you want when you have a lot of players that you feel are capable of making the 53. Shoot, being with the guys like George Pickens, being with guys like I see these flow, Mingo, Quest, all those guys, they made it easy for me. Um, those veterans made it very, very easy for me. And shoot, I'm I'm thankful for them. >> All right, thanks, Carson. >> Thank y'all so much. God bless. >> Jordan, how would you kind of assess your performance tonight? >> Um, play I feel like I did good. Um, obviously there are things you need to clean up. Um, like the one I threw to Trey, when I could have just ran and got the first. Other than that, feel like I did pretty good. >> Expanding beyond just overall preseason and training camp, how would you assess how you played? >> Uh, see, feel like I did what I was supposed to do. Um, feel like I showed up when my name was called. Um, I feel like I did all the right things in the place. Um, so, we'll see what happens. >> Seeing a guy like Hudson get a chance tonight to shine at receiver, kind of show that the depth is on this team. >> Yes, um, shout out to him. Um, just being in the right place at the right time, and being able to come down with those footballs, and make a great catch for the team. Um, it's awesome to see, especially from a young guy. >> I know you said that what you do in the dark will come into the light earlier this week, but just how encouraged are you by what you put on film this preseason? >> Um, shoot, man, I don't think nobody can knock my uh, courage, man, my confidence, no nothing. Uh, I mean, I look in the mirror every morning. Um, and I ask myself, do I really want to do this? And I do, so. Uh, this whole preseason, I feel like I did great. Uh, but I feel like obviously there are things to learn from, but uh, from this preseason to last preseason, I feel like I did a hell of a job. >> What did you make of Sam's second half from the sidelines? >> Great. Uh, Sam played great. Um, shoot, I was out there rooting rooting him on. Um, you know, same thing we tell each other before uh, all three of these preseason games. This our first year being on the same team together, so squat down, and show them. Good. Thank y'all. >> Jordan, obviously a big night. How would you assess yourself tonight? >> Uh, man, just a blessing. Uh Hate that we lost, but uh man, it was a good game. Good hard fought win I mean good hard fought loss, but uh man, we just got to come stronger. We'll We'll build on this. Say it again. Yes, sir. I mean not as of right now. Yeah. Uh I'm I'm focused on making this team. Uh that's that's where my priority is at. Uh but if the opportunity comes and I and I get cut uh I will figure it out when it get here. Uh I mean we'll we'll figure it out when we get there. I don't really got no question on that yet. I ain't really worried about college uh football. I'm in the NFL, so that's what I'm focused on right now. >> Jordan, speaking of making this team, what was going through your mind tonight? You had a lot of great plays back to back. >> Uh really just man, showing them that I can I could be here. I could play on this level and that's really all I was worried about. Uh not worried about trying not to focus on anybody else's success and and really worried about what I could do when I get in the game. >> What do you think it was going to be more important to the coaching staff? You doing that and catching the touchdown or on the next play making the stop on on coverage? >> Uh probably uh making the stop on coverage. Most definitely. I think I think they know I can score touchdowns. >> Do you feel like this training camp was building up to this moment and how how why do you think you were drafted for just this big game today? >> I mean it's it's been a a pretty rocky uh camp. Uh just been keeping my head down, but I mean I just been praying to God, man, and and he allowed me to come out here and perform and and do my uh one and eleven, so that's what I did. >> So, how do you stay patient though cuz you know different seems like in preseason games get different guys get different opportunities. >> Say it again. >> Hard to stay patient, know, Cam Brown has a couple of big games and then, you know, it just seems like in preseason, different nights, different guys get a chance to shine. >> I mean, if you go look at my resume, uh I I done played a lot behind a lot of big-time guys, uh Quinton Johnson, uh Didi Davis, Tay Barber, so I mean, I know what it I know what it come with, uh not being the guy right away. So, I mean, just just keeping your head down, believing in God, and and knowing your ability. Uh so, I mean, I know I'm a dog. I know what I bring to the table, and man, I I I put that on display tonight. >> How many friends and family do you have here tonight? >> Probably over 50. Yeah. Thank y'all. >> Sam, how would you assess the overall way you played tonight? >> Uh yeah, it was fun. It was fun to kind of get back in the game there in the fourth quarter. Hey, we didn't end it the right way. Um it was fun to be in a competitive game like that, and um have a chance to win it there. Uh hate we didn't pull it out, but um there's some good stuff to learn from, for sure. I think so. I mean, I feel like I've had a good camp. Uh I feel like I'm playing some good ball right now. I feel confident in the system. Um and then, you know, I think us and the the guys we're out there with we're developing some good chemistry as far as, you know, us and the O line, us and the receivers. Um so, it's I thought it was a good preseason. Um and, you know, I'm happy about where where the way I performed. >> Preseason is interesting because of different guys. It seems to change about each week. And tonight, it was quite something at receiver. Does that speak to uh the depth that they have in the talent that's in that unit? >> Yeah, we we we have a lot of talent in that receiver room. Um and, you know, I hate that you can only keep so many guys cuz there's a lot of young guys on this roster right now that deserve to make the team. Um and, you know, the a lot of those guys made plays throughout the preseason, and it makes our job fun to go out there in the preseason with a great group of young receivers cuz that's who we're going to be out there with. Um and they made plays for me and Joel all preseason, so it's been fun to work with those guys. >> How would you kind of describe your relationship with Joe and just how you guys have handled this competition with each other? >> It's been great. Joe's been great, man. We've We've pushed each other. We have a great relationship. At the end of the day, you know, we're we're part of the same team. Um you know, obviously we both want to, you know, win a competition or you know, at the end of the day we both want to play at some point. Um we both want to start in this league. We're both after the same thing, so it's been fun to you know, push each other and I feel like we've made each other better. Um and that's the main thing and um it's never anything personal. Um and Joe's been great. >> How challenging is it this time of the year to deal with the uncertainty that comes with not knowing exactly what's going to happen here? >> Yeah, you never know. Um but you just You just got to take it one day at a time and put your best foot forward and um you know, you got to do your best. Um and you got to trust that God has a good plan for you no matter where that is, whether that's here or somewhere else. Um but you can't You can't You got to control what you can control. Um and that's how you approach every single day and um try to put your best foot forward. >> How did sound like playing Adams in the year two tonight? >> Play was great. Um I've enjoyed getting to know Clayton. Um he's got a bright future as a as a play caller in this league and um it was cool to get that opportunity to, you know, to play with him calling the plays and he's called it throughout training camp a little bit and um he was great. There weren't any mishaps out there and um hate we couldn't win it for him. Um I'm not making any of the decisions, so you know, I I did I did the best I could. Um and at the end of the day, no matter what it is, I can sleep at night knowing I did the best I could. Um and that's, you know, kind of what I live by. Um but you know, I think you know, you That's all you can do in life. You know, do do the best you can each and every day and um let them decide what they want to do. >> Sideline was pretty hyped after you You that two-point conversion run in. What was just your reaction seeing the whole sideline kind of running out there to celebrate with you? >> Yeah, it was pretty cool. We have a cool group of guys here. Um the bond here is, you know, different than any other place I've been. Um and I've been around a little bit and um it just speaks to the great culture they have here in this building and you know, a lot of people don't care about the preseason, but um you can tell by the energy on the sideline that no matter if it's preseason or regular season, we want to win. Um and that's just the culture that they built here and I'm just happy to be a part of it. Uh yeah, I got my hat on right here. Um I'm ready to go. Um but I think Bill turns it around this year. Um I have a lot of respect for him and um I I I hope we get it done. Thank you, guys. >> Sam, two sacks for you in the last two preseason games. How do you feel like you closed out this >> Um I would think I did pretty good. Uh like a lot of people emphasize like I'm I'm in a position where I'm interviewing for all 31 other teams, also. So, um I had to basically show that like last season wasn't the the defining aspect of Sam, you know? So, see what happens. >> What do you feel like you showed in that interview? >> That I'm back, you know? Uh after um what, 2 years now of my uh surgery, I feel like ready, ready to compete at a high level and and you know, take charge, I guess. >> As the staff is mulling over their decisions over the next 48 hours, what's your kind of pitch of why you should be here still? >> Um there's really no pitch. Um they want me, they want me. If they don't, they don't. I don't know. Cuz like I just leave it in God's hand, you know? I got a praying mother uh and she tell me to worry less and work more. So, that's what I do. See, busting, ain't it? >> Ooh! >> How do you see yourself continuing to help this team? >> Of course. Um I know I can help this team the way I practice, the way I come out every day in the tackle. And just the way I revamp my mindset. I learned about alter egos uh recently from Chad in our team meeting. So every day on before practice, before I step on the field, I write down like my alter ego. But I can't say it because I don't want to like it's a person that's a very bad person that used to kill people. But like I don't know. Like the mindset that I have like when I walk on that field, it's just like this person that is unstoppable and and this just want to I don't know. I don't know how to put it. >> So it's the alter ego?

title: Schottenheimer, Jerry Jones, & Exclusive Interviews From the Preseason Finale | Countdown To Kickoff
text: Go. The dream brought them here. The competition kept them here. Now there's one more chance to stay here. Under the lights in front of Cowboys Nation, roster spots hang in the balance. Tonight, they're not promised a place on the team. They try to earn one. Countdown to kickoff. Countdown to cutdowns starts now. The Dallas Cowboys presentation of Countdown to Kickoff presented by AT&T is sponsored by Bank of America. What would you like the power to do? Reliant, official energy provider of the Dallas Cowboys. Yeti, official licensed Yeti Cowboys gear, available at Stadium Pro Shops, Concession, and on Yeti.com. And by AT&T, connecting changes everything. It's time for some Friday night football here at AT&T Stadium in Arlington as the Cowboys are back home to take on the New Orleans Saints in preseason game number three. First time in front of the home fans here this 2026 preseason. And this is countdown to kickoff. Bill Jones along with Vicky Spagnola. And as usual, right off the top joined by Cowboys head coach Brian Shottenheimer. And it is great to be home. You've been home for about a week now and got some practices in at the Star in Fris in front of fans. Great to be back here in Arlington, too. >> It's amazing. And uh you know, we love we love playing here. We love the home field advantage that we get and uh the guys are feeling it and uh they're ready to go tonight. >> And you've got a few days here before you have to make your roster cuts and it's always tough. I thought you said something interesting earlier in the week when somebody asked you how training camp went and you said it was really good. And then you went on to say uh that if you compared our roster now, lay it down next to where we were last year, how much the roster has improved and in different ways, some from within also. >> Yeah, I think you know I I never really like to look back, Mickey, but you're right. I mean it it just it's real. It's fact. So I'm not going to say that it's not. And I think that's a testament to to Jerry and Steven and Will Mcclelay and all of our personnel guys that work so hard at this. We've just we've made a lot of, you know, really really good moves. We've got great young men that are really good football players. And I think that's one of the reasons why you see us playing in these preseason games when you're sitting 29, 30 guys sometimes and you're still noticing the play style and the physicality and all those things that we believe in. I saw it should have be a picture on the bench and looks like they're not playing, but it was Quinnon Williams, Rashad Garry, and Kenny Clark sitting together and I'm thinking, okay, this time last year these guys weren't here and that was one example of what you've done with your roster without a doubt. And then again, you name those three, then you bring in Caleb DS, and you bring in Dwinners, and you bring in Malachi Lawrence, and uh just so many different pieces that we've brought in that we're really excited about. And uh um it's a it's a noticeable difference. >> So, one of the things we'll be looking at tonight are your quarterbacks, the backup quarterbacks, Joe Milton, uh Sam How playing for that backup spot. How will you handle them today? And then what do you want to see from them going forward? Yeah, Joe will start. Um, so it's a lot like last week in Arizona. They'll both play a half. Um, it's still very much a quarterback competition. You know, I think, uh, Joe's played really well in both preseason games. Sam finished strong against Seattle. Uh, Arizona didn't get as many opportunities. We're running the ball really well. Uh, but when you factor in every practice and the padded work that we did out in Oxnard and that we've even done here, uh, those guys are battling neck andneck. And so, uh, we want to see him move the football team and put them in the end zone and, uh, get us in and out of right plays and good checks and things like that. And, uh, um, it's going to be fun to watch. >> Now, you are 2 and 0 as an offensive play caller, uh, this preseason. Uh, are you going to make it 3 and 0 as an offensive play caller yourself tonight or what? >> Well, that's a great lead in, but uh, no. Uh, Clayton Adams is going to call the plays on offense and, uh, I could not be more excited for him. He deserves this opportunity. Uh we believe in developing our coaches and um you know we we want these guys to all have great success and uh it's a great opportunity for him. Uh I'm going to keep my mouth shut and try not to get involved but uh he's worked his butt off to get ready for this and uh he'll do a great job. So it's going to be fun and I get to again really dive into some of the finer details. I'll be really watching a lot of the personnel matchups and >> you know what we really need is you joining us on the broadcast tonight. That's what we really need. Well, I mean, you guys are the right people to ask, you know, so uh my language sometimes doesn't fit for TV. Uh but I'd probably work on that for you guys. >> So, you've got um some log jams at a couple positions you're going to have to make tough, uh decisions at wide receiver, uh running back. I think those are two of them. So, what do you look for tonight or do you have an idea of where you're almost there and maybe somebody can change your mind tonight? Yeah, we have kind of uh, you know, we keep track of reps throughout training camp. You know, we know how many reps this guy has in team and how many this guy has in one-on- ones and how many game reps they have. And so, you know, we want to kind of balance out the reps, if you will. And, okay, well, let's make sure before we have to make some of these really, really difficult decisions that, hey, this guy got a fair shot in terms of comparing him to this other player. And, uh, a lot goes into it. There's a lot of time and effort spent on it. And, uh, it's not a perfect science, but we feel like we can do that tonight. And there's one guy I think everybody's asking questions about the running back position. Uh Malik Davis. He he just seems to had his hand up in the air and said, "Hey, don't forget about me. You might have all these other little pieces, but I'm still pretty good." >> Yeah. And uh again, I've talked about Malik all the time. He really just grew up. last year he was in a tough situation where we moved on from him and then you know we came brought him back in training camp and um I think it truly shows the maturation process of a guy that was out for a little while and said hey I never want to be in this situation again I'm going to capitalize and maximize my opportunities and uh he's done that and uh he's a excellent football player in multiple phases not just offense but also on special teams and uh so proud of him. All right, Brian Shottenheimer, we appreciate it and enjoy the game tonight. Hope Clayton Adams calls good plays. >> Me, too. >> And we continue with Countdown to Kickoff in just a moment. We're be joined by Jerry Jones, the Cowboys owner, president, general manager, when she's done talking with Christy Scales in just a moment. This segment is brought to you by Dr. Pepper. Raise your Dr. Pepper glass to America's team. It's a pepper thing. Preseason game number three. Countdown to kickoff. It's the Cowboys and the New Orleans Saints. Cowboys 2 and 0 so far this preseason. Bill Jones along with Mickey Spagnola. Now joined by Cowboys owner president and general manager Jerry Jones. It's great to be back at AT&T Stadium. Football season is here. We got the Jerry Jones Classic at the Star in Frisco tomorrow. High school football Highland Park in Lewisville. It's a great time of year, Jerry. Well, when that what a better uh classic that morning when I wake up, it's like Dracula popping up after 100 years. My bowl game is happening out here today and I barely touched the ground on my way out there. I look forward to it so much. All kidding aside, I really do like that uh what we're doing having those great high school teams and these are two of the best starting the season in high school. So, we're excited about that. is just uh so uh not only excited about that, but excited the fact that we'll have this game in the can. Our coaches evaluating that tape and starting that as uh we go out there for that bowl game tomorrow night. And um that's exciting cuz I love the way this team has some really, if you will, battles, unanswered questions as to what we're going to do with the depth. So, you have two days until you have to go from 90 to 53. What are your thoughts on where your roster is overall right now? >> Well, I think we've got um and it's reflected in this way we played these two preseason games so far. Uh this is outstanding depth that we're dealing with here and we've got some real talent. Uh the young players have borne out. They have not disappointed at all. Uh we've got a couple of tough two or three decisions to make, but still uh I love what preseason has shown us about our depth. Now preseason didn't miss uh the play of the guys that are going to be counted on for most of the success and that's been outstanding as well. And so this group that we're having to make those cuts in were the ones that pushed our starting players and the players that are going to get 70 80% of the time. Uh they pushed them at a level that I frankly is the best I've seen in years. >> So your evaluation, you got to see those frontline players in two scrimmages. The last one against these Saints and then against the Rams. So when you saw those guys out there, your feeling about this ro this team right now? >> Well, each player at each position, but each player had coming into camp some things that you wanted to see how how they're handling it, how they're uh playing in those areas. Uh it could be a receiver and it could be some work and uh his confidence. Uh Flora is an example of that. He's been outstanding. That's exactly the trajectory that you'd want to see from where he came from last year as an example. So, those are the kinds of things we've seen and uh it looks good. So, one of the things that has taken place, and I think sometimes it gets overlooked from the trades you made, uh, the veteran free agents you signed, but you've s kind of grown from within with some young guys that have stepped up from last year and came back from injuries that we only saw for a few games last year. Now, they're full-time, healthy, and ready to go. >> Yeah. And one of the things you've got to bet on some of the positives happening uh ahead of schedule when uh you start the year. You got to kind of project and bet that the younger players will get better. And then you also have to with your veteran players anticipate how much drop off you might have from the time you're in training camp to the time you get to the Super Bowl. So that projection of having those players getting better after they played 17 games, the young ones, and having the uh the the kind of the solid evaluation of veteran players, but with an understanding that uh that playoff is two college football seasons away. And so there's a lot happened during that time, too. So, it's me measuring or or projecting a little bit where you're going to be at a point of the time. And then again, we all know how important it is to win these games as we go uh toward the playoffs. Uh the Cowboys over the last 15 years, I think we're either sixth or seventh of the winningest team in the NFL of 32 teams. Uh, but that has to uh take into consideration what kind of shape were you in when you got to the playoffs and what are you doing there as far as the guys that won those games in that season. We need to get better at that. >> Know you feel great about uh Dak Prescott, where he is in his career, the the level he's been playing at. Uh your backup quarterback situation. Brian Shottenheimer told us that Joe Milton will get the start tonight. And Sam, how what are you what are you seeing as far as the two backups go? Oh, I hope Joe I for everybody I hope Joe can uh continue uh with his uh how slow how slowed down the game. What does that mean slow the game down? It means that he's just more comfortable with what was fast coming at him. It's now gotten so familiar that it looks slow and he plays that way. He had a game like that the other day, the best one I've ever seen him play. And so if we can build on that, uh, then man, that is encouraging. And of course, I think that we could end up here in the best shape we've been in in years, uh, at our backup quarterback, which is critical. And I think one of the things when you're talking about the backup quarterback, cuz as we know, once you start getting into game preparation during the season, they don't get many snaps. So they got to rely on their experience. When it comes to a Milton who hasn't really started the game in the NFL, I think there's a trust factor that you have to be able to evaluate going forward. Well, it's trust, but it's this. If you haven't seen how to use him, the kind of things you're going to ask the quarterback to do, if you haven't seen evidence of that during this time, pre-season, then it impacts what you are unsure about in the regular season should you're needed. So, there's a very pointed reason for seeing some good things done because that will impact how he's used should he be needed. Well, it's going to be fun watching these guys tonight and then two weeks from Sunday at the New York Giants, Sunday Night Football, it's going to even be even more fun then. Jerry, we appreciate it. >> Bill, it's uh the old adage of whatever we see when we open up against the Giants is what we put in out here tonight and what we put in in training camp. If you didn't put it in, it won't come out against the Giants. >> There. There you go. That's the theme of this training camp from Jerry Jones. We appreciate it, Jerry. And when we come back here on Countdown to Kickoff, we're talking safeties. This segment brought to you by Dr. Pepper. Raise your Dr. Pepper glass to America's team. It's a Pepper thing. This segment brought to you by Ashley Hometore, the official furniture store of the Dallas Cowboys. We're counting you down to kickoff tonight. Preseason game number three at beautiful AT&T Stadium. Dallas Cowboys and New Orleans Saints. Bill Jones with Mickey Spagnola. And now joined by Nick Eatman, who we call our first round draft pick here. You're always the first one to come on after the head coach and the owner, Nick. >> Sounds like a third round pick really. But either either way is great. Now, speaking of first round picks, how about Caleb DS? Here's a guy that he's only played eight snaps in the preseason. Hasn't played a regular season game, but you know what? He's already sounding like a veteran. >> At the end of the day, we are all pushing to win a Super Bowl, but at the end of the day, um, somebody said it best today. We can only have the best day today. Um, so we can't win the Super Bowl right now. We're just trying to have the best day that we can today. And that's the same thing for myself. Uh, I'm trying to accomplish my goals and be great in myself. Uh, and today is just being about being great today. That's all I can focus on. Now, if Caleb DS is going to be great today, it's going to have to be right now as in pregame because that's about all we're going to see from him. But guys, I just love the way that his maturity just pops off every single time you you talk to him. And I love what he says. The goal is there. It's the Super Bowl. It's the same for every team, but you can't get it today. So, don't overlook, you know, the the daily grind of making sure you're going to meetings, making sure that it's the best practice, it's the best game, because you do all that, then you can get to the big goal. You know, one of the things I think we've seen from him, Nick, during training camp, his versatility, like he'll start off on the first nickel in the slot, but at some point he's back at a deep safety. And that's invaluable when you can have different positions with the same guy. >> Exactly. You know, it reminds me of a tight end on the other side, a tight end that can create so many mismatches and sometimes they can line out a receiver, sometimes they will block. Are they going to beat the corner every time? No. Are they going to beat the defensive end? No. But they can do it. It's the same with Caleb DS. He can cover the slot. He can cover on the outside. He can go up and run support. And and I think just having him on the field is one of those offsets to those types of tight ends that create mismatches on the other side. >> All right. Uh this you look at the safety depth chart and there's a big free agent signing in Jaylen Thompson. You got Malik Hooker coming back. You got PJ Lock, another veteran coming in here. Kind of a forgotten guy back there at the back end of the defense. is a guy who is a special teams demon projected to be that on this team and that's Maris Bell >> right I mean this safety position went from a need obviously because they they they addressed it in free agency and then Caleb down landed right in their lap but like to your point Maris Bell is a Swiss Army knife that could do a lot of different things and then you've got you know Elijah Clark Julius Wood so this position went from a spot where it's a definitely a need and now there's some good players that are probably going to get released. >> And I was just going to ask you that because in two days they got to trim that safety position down. And when you think that Downs can do both, it's like he's not just the slot corner, he's a deep safety also. And then you got these young guys that stepped up and Wood should be able to play tonight. He's been out. Uh it makes it complicated. >> You know, one guy that that's caught, you know, his attention, uh Darren Woodson. Darren Woodson said I got a chance to talk to him and he was like who's Julius Wood who's this guy like you you know he just he's he's kind of one of those guys that you just he pops off the screen and so you know Elijah Clark the same way. So th those two guys I don't know how they they figure out how to keep them or you know they'd love to keep one of them on the practice squad but I think this is the year where there's going to be some guys that that they hope to get on the practice squad that are just going to get claimed by other teams. It's that deep of a roster. Well, and it's going to be interesting to see how these guys are utilized. The ones that are getting the playing time are utilized in Christian Parker's defense as well. Nick Eatman, we appreciate it. Getting you ready for the Cowboys and the Saints tonight. And this segment brought to you by Ashley of the Dallas Cowboys. When we come back, Charlotte Jones joins us. We're talking about a variety of things with Charlotte next on Countdown to Kickoff. Each year, more than 5,000 Arlington ISD fifth and eighth grade art students tour the Dallas Cowboys art collection at AT&T Stadium, courtesy of the Gan and Jerry Jones family Arlington Youth Foundation. Each student creates a work of art inspired by their visit. And tonight, AT&T Stadium has highlighted the work of the fifth, eighth, and senior students who participated with a curated art display located at entry E. The goal of the Cowboys Arlington ISD art program presented by Waterburger is to instill an appreciation for art in students at a pivotal grade level. Congratulations to all of them as we countdown to kickoff here. Cowboys and Saints tonight. Bill Jones with Mickey Spagnola. And now joined by Cowboys co-owner and chief brand officer Charlotte Jones. That is a great thing that the Cowboys do with Arlington ISD every year. >> You know, it is so exciting and that program has continued to grow and we awarded almost $10,000 in scholarships to the seniors. So, every fifth grader gets to participate and those that continue to engage in the program have scholarship opportunities to take them into hopefully what might be their career, certainly their passion into the future. So, it's very exciting to be able to lure them in, use a little football to lure them in to have an appreciation for art and find their talents. >> Well, uh let's talk about some talented football players who are the girls flag football is one of the booming sports in this country and the Cowboys have been very very much a part of that. >> Yes. You know, it is hard to believe that just two years ago, there were only about 600 girls playing girls flag. Now there's over 4,000 girls playing girls flag and that's about 220 schools across the state of Texas. And we are so excited about the growth here in this state and we get to highlight a little bit at halftime because we had our first ever state championship and one of our locals over there, Rockwell Heath, won the big title. Um I know um Houston was probably sad to see us grab that first title, but you know, we like to do that. And if it takes the girls to do it, boy, more power to them. >> And how much more can this grow? Because I see where some of the colleges now are getting into flag football as a team sport and giving out scholarships also. >> Absolutely, Mickey. title: Kelvin Sheppard Exclusive Training Camp Interview | Detroit Lions
text: Join now by Lions defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard ahead of the 2026 season. Coach, when you had a chance [music] to go back and watch the tape, what were the three focus points for you that you wanted to implement heading into this season? >> Uh probably the three biggest things was limiting the explosive plays primarily in the pass game. Um I would say the second is creating a system that's adjustable [music] and adaptable for everyone, not specific players. A kind of a plug and play thing where we always have answers within formation, within drives, first half, [music] second half, adjustable things as the the game flow, as the season flow. >> [music] >> Um whether that be injury, personnel, whatever it is, the ship never stops moving. And then the third, which >> is the most important, just making sure we continue to create our identity. Uh and that's playing a violent, [music] physical brand of football. >> Hey, there we go. There we go, guys. >> When you go from linebacker coach to defensive coordinator, how is it now different implementing all of those things in this [music] position? >> Well, to be honest, and you guys could talk to AG and Dan, I've always had a holistic view on things. [music] Um making sure I mastered kind of my baby first, year year one as outside linebackers. >> Then the next three years a broader span with all the OLBs. And then them just putting more [music] and more responsibilities on my plate as I went year to year coaching the edge players although I was the linebacker coach. Putting more people in my room, involving you more in the game plan. So, that's why I've been afforded a tremendous opportunity uh due to the leadership here under Dan. Uh giving me certain platforms. So, I was kind of not new to seeing things [music] as a whole um coming from being a position coach. >> And you got a front row seat. How has the defense [music] evolved from the time you got here as a coach >> Yeah. >> to what it is now? >> Uh it's completely changed. This [music] This is where and things take time. That's what I tell everybody. Um even in my first year, it was my fifth year here being with the Lions, but you get new players every year. You get and you got to make sure that they can go out and execute. It's one thing for us, I tell the staff all the time, to sit up in a room in the AC with our fine sharpie pens and all this drawing up all this stuff, but it's about what can the players retain and [music] more importantly what can they go out and execute at a high level. >> When you talk about picking talent, I want to pick your brain a little bit in the film room. >> When you're looking at, okay, this is the needs heading into 2026 ahead of the draft, >> how do you evaluate what you guys need? >> Just really trying to take a step back from what we saw through the months and months of self-scout leading into the draft process, free agency, and just being honest and being honest with the front office starting with Brad, telling them what we feel our areas of concern, and then what [music] we feel are the biggest needs, and then what do we see that type player, player A being, player B being, all right, we want to be specific at certain spots to what we're looking for, and then ultimately just trusting those guys to do their job just like they trust us as coaches to do ours. >> What type of players, I want to get your philosophy on this. Different [music] teams look at different things when it comes to the nickel corner position and the intangibles that they're specifically looking for. What are you looking for when you want to bring one to this defense? >> Um, that that that's kind of a two-fold question from the standpoint of everybody wants, you look at our roster right now, a player like Brian Branch, that's kind of the prototypical nickel right now. A guy that can play not only in the pass game but the run game, but those don't just fall off trees. You know, you look around the league, how many of those are out there? So, just finding out [music] what do players do well, that's going back to the self-scout, and seeing how do we put these players in optimal [music] position. So, we right now have multiple people serving that role, it's just a matter of what's the situation, what are we [music] looking for a per that type package, per that type play, and making sure we put the right player in that spot. >> Players that are doing things well, the linebacker [music] room might be one of the deeper position groups heading into this season. How would you evaluate where that group's at right now? >> Yeah, I may be a little biased. And everybody feel Ham in the D-staff room he has the hardest [music] job. Coaching linebackers for me. But he does a tremendous job. It starts with Shawn Dion [music] Hamilton. Uh the leadership that he instills, the mentality, uh the no-nonsense. These guys know he's there to push them and make them better. And I think they push each other at the same time. Um I mean they are deep. We we can go all the way to our fifth, sixth backer. Guys like Amon-Ra [music] that just showed up, Bachie that just showed up. Whatever I told Dan the other day, I trust these guys to go in the game and function at a high level. And we don't believe in drop-off defensively [music] and especially in that room. >> Somebody you trust, I think with the entire defense, your quarterback on that side of the ball in Jack Campbell. I had a chance to ask him what it's like from his perspective on the headset. I want to get your answer on that. >> I'll be curious to see what he said about that. So let me know when that interview finally gets aired. But Jack tells everybody, you better be ready. These guys is getting it for the first time in the preseason. Jack's a very intense coach. Um I believe the players can not only hear you, but they [music] can feel you. And they know when it's real. So just me and Jack are in lockstep at this point going into year four for him. Coaching him as a linebacker, coaching last year first year coordinator. Jack knows my thought process. He knows the whys behind why I'm calling it. He's just not repeating [music] what he hears on the gridiron. He understands why. And he's able to relate that to the players in game, [music] in practice. And that helps a ton. >> I've seen that intensity out on the practice field. You're not afraid to challenge guys like Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jamo on the offensive side of the ball. Why is that important to do that out here? >> Because [music] they're real guys. And real guys want to be challenged and pushed. I tell everybody, you look at a player like Aidan Hutchinson, he's never a finished product. That player wants to be coached just like a rookie undrafted player. And you got to have the ability to push them and challenge them. But it starts with respect >> and earning these guys' respect to be able to have that type of relationship. And we're a family. Guys like Waymo and Saint, I've been in this with them from the beginning. So, those are my little brothers. >> All right, [music] last one. When all is said and done at the end of the season, how do you want this defense to be remembered? >> I want us to be remembered [music] as a reason why we were able to help our team propel to that to that next level or that next step. And when people turn on our tape, our identity always speaks [music] for us, not our words. >> Awesome, Coach. I appreciate it. >> Thank you. Appreciate you.
