title: Players and Coach Hafley meet with the media after #ATLvsMIA
text: to make. >> Jeff, what did you learn about maybe yourself going through your first training camp as head coach, your first preseason, and now as you get ready for your first regular season game? >> Yeah, I I just I learned a lot of things. I mean, I don't I don't even know where to start with that. I think you you probably learn every single day. Um after every week, you kind of when the players have a day off, you try to evaluate yourself. You try to evaluate the schedule. You try to think about what you would do different, what you liked. Um but you got to remain true to yourself. when things get hard, when things don't come easy, you can't flinch and you can't veer off the plan and you got to trust your staff. Um, and you and you got to you got to really communicate with your players. Um, I I really I like the camp that we had and I think it's a really really good starting point. >> Coach Chris Bell made his preseason debut tonight. Just talk about what you saw from him and how exciting you were to see him in an actual game after all all the injuries has he's had to battle through. Yeah. Um, have to go back and really watch the film to really hone in on him. I know he had a a bunch of opportunities to catch the ball. I know he made he made some of those catches. Um, I just think the way he's worked, the way Kyle's worked with him and Todd, our strength coach, and obviously Kyle, our trainer, how hard he's pushed himself to give him a chance to get back where he's at right now. I think a lot of people didn't give him a chance to get back until a lot later, which is why he probably was drafted where he is. um he's attacked it and those guys did a great job with him and I think what you're still seeing right now is he hasn't played a lot of football and he needs to do that and it's the muscle memory and it's the movement and it's the suddenness but what a cool deal for him to come out and try to you know get some action tonight which was really important for him because he hasn't done very much. >> Was it very intentional to get him that first play? >> Um it was intentional to get him involved early. the read and the coverage probably dictated that more, but we definitely wanted to try to get him involved early because he was going to be on a pitch count. So, your answer is yes, sooner than later. >> Jeff, this might be a question for him. I think we're getting him later, but uh for Chris. >> Yeah, >> but uh I think he took a hit on one of those targets and just kind of like gathered himself for a minute and bounced up. How important is it for him to take hits like that in the preseason as he's working his way back? Yeah, I think anybody who's played the game and I I think that's just as important. He He's got to get hit again and he has not been for a long time. You know, we didn't practice very much with him and he was in a non-cont jersey for a long time. So, probably shook that off and and said, "All right, I'm ready to go now." I think you'll probably get a good answer from him on that. >> Jeeoff, if I could follow up my earlier question, it's going to be a process for a young team like this. Will it also be a process for you as a first year NFL? Yeah, for sure. I mean, I think for everybody it's going to be a process, but I think we have I think we have a very good process that is started and I think we have a foundation that is laid and you know, I think when we go out here and and even tonight, right, like you want to win in everything that you do, like everything. And you know, we obviously couldn't get that done tonight, and I could list off why. Um, but at the same time, this process has got to be strong, and there's going to be some ups and downs, and there's going to be some great moments, and there's going to be moments that we have to learn from. But the whole key to this year is doing everything we can to win football games, but making sure we do it right. So, the foundation's right and the process is right. So, win or lose, it's we're going like this, right? And again, I I want to win in everything that we do, but I want to make sure that as we build this year, we're doing it the right way with no shortcuts because the goal here is to sustain success and take no shortcuts. And it is going to be hard and we're going to work hard and our staff's going to work hard and our players are going to work hard. And I am really really excited to start honing in and game planning and getting ready for our first game. >> Jeff, can you give us updates on two guys? >> Sure. >> Uh Quinn Yers and Jacob Rodriguez. >> Yeah. Um Quinn, we tried to get back into practice this week, but never truly felt comfortable enough to move around um to be able to go out and play in a really a live setting. Um and then Jacob, you said Jacob. Jacob, same thing. Jacob didn't practice last few days. Uh Jacob will be dayto day, but but he he was not able to play today. >> Coach, talk about how satisfied you were with Miami's defense early on, specifically forcing turnovers against what was the bulk of Atlanta's starting roster. >> Yeah, I think for, you know, I told the guys today when we went out there, I mean, what an opportunity, you know, their starters, guys on our team trying to make the team, guys on our team trying to make other teams to put on tape against their starters. And I think we forced two fumbles and had an interception. And really, even on that first big play, if we just set the edge, we're off the field. And clearly, we got to coach it better and play it better. But I just love how hard they played and how confident they played. And I think a lot of those guys took advantage of their opportunity um against a lot of starters. So, I am proud of them. I'm probably more proud in the second half. We challenged them. And I thought our guys on defense and offense, I I thought did a really nice job in the second half. And if you watch the sideline, um, after big plays, it was like everybody was excited. And then the even cooler part was we had a chance, right? We missed a couple a drop here, an overthrow here, a penalty here, and everybody was picking each other up. And it was really cool as I watched in that second half to watch the team kind of come together. And those were the things that are going to be really important to us this year. >> What ultimately led to the decision to rest starters tonight? And how comfortable are you having them play just the one series is crazy? >> Yeah. I I mean it is as I went into this thing it wasn't the plan, right? But it's kind of like what we just talked about as you go through you you just can't write out your plan and say, "Hey, I'm I'm sticking to this no matter what." We had a bunch of injuries and we became super thin in a lot of positions and um you know, we just felt with the injuries. And then the other thing is we we still looked and we talked all week, Sully and I and the staff um there was a lot of evaluation left and we felt what was best for our team right now was to give those guys the eval and to make sure that we get healthy so we can really get those guys ready for next week in week one. Um and and we just felt that was the best decision for us for our football team. tacky velocity injuries. >> Uh both. I I I mean we we had to have guys that could play in the game. Um so we just we felt like we wanted to get them in or um you know we really were down to I think two linebackers for the rest of the game because you got Brooks out, you got Rodriguez out, you got Ronnie out. So you got to have people to play in the game. They were healthy. Um, and I thought they did a really nice job. >> Felt like in the second half Rowski was not afraid to air the ball out. Talk about his confidence and how it's grown ever since the team resigned him. >> Yeah, I thought him and Cam both did a night I thought they were better today. I thought the ball came out on time. I thought the offensive line gave them better protection. They looked more in rhythm. Um, and then you mentioned Grank just the toughness of some of those pull down runs that he had and it was unfortunate. You're going in to score and high snap with a lot of heat on it. kind of got bent backwards. So, I just I respect his toughness and I saw improvement from both of those guys today. >> You have some guys who have not been here very long, including Hunter just arriving. Um, how does that figure into day? How do you evaluate a guy? >> It's hard. There's limited tape. So you go you got to go on what you saw and you gota what you saw in the past and then you go got to go on what we were able to do today which is another reason we felt like we needed to play a lot of these guys. So you know we'll get together and we'll watch this tape. We'll watch it tonight. Um we we'll evaluate it again in the morning and and then there's going to be some hard decisions to make. But that's not easy. We had a lot in the last two weeks. We had a lot of new players show up um which is preseason in the NFL. Last question. >> Jeff, you went on with Stephen A, I think a while ago. It just came out this past week. Uh, and you had this quote where success the seasons can be measured not in wins and losses, but on development as a competitor though, like how difficult is it to balance that, you know, wanting to win and the desire to win with knowing realistically where the team is at this stage and wanting to keep building to something. >> Yeah. Um, success is not, look, let me say this. We and I want to win everything that we do, but success is not just defined by winning. Winning for sure, right? That's why we play the game. And I think every competitor wants to win in everything that we do. But it's kind of like what I was just talking about before. Um, we we're going to compete. I want to win everything that we do. I've said that over and over, but at the same time, we need to make sure that this foundation and the process is built the right way. And like I was saying, that there's no shortcuts because it's bigger than that right now. And those are the things that are really important as we move this thing forward and we build and we find out who we have what we have because we want to get back on top. And to do that, you got to go through some hard stuff with competing in mind to win in everything that we do. but keeping the main thing our process in the detail and the toughness and not taking any shortcuts and not flinching along the way regardless of what happens. So at the end of the year we can look back and say this foundation is strong and we're not going away cuz look out we're coming. You understand what I'm saying? So I think that kind of got lost in probably my conversation. It's not just it. There's a lot of things that are bigger than that, but I can look you in the eye and tell you we are going to do everything we can to win every single >> You guys good? >> Sorry. How did it feel to finally be back out there first, late November? >> It felt great just to step back out there on the field, you know, for my first NFL game being in Miami Stadium. It felt pretty good. So, I'm just blessed, you know, had an opportunity to be out there, you know, some with my with my brothers. >> How long did you know that first ball was coming your way? >> Um, I've been knowing the whole week. I'm not going to lie. Uh, we've been, uh, we had this play, we had put this play in. It's called Well, yeah, we put this play in, but um, I knew the whole week, uh, me and the quarterback, we was talking about, you know, if if he's pressed or if he's off, he was going to come to me in the boundary. So, you know, I've been knowing. >> Chris, there's a couple plays. So there's I think practice on uh Wednesday, Tuesday or Wednesday >> and then >> a play tonight where you got hit and kind of stay on the ground for a second before >> getting up. What are those moments like as you are learning to trust your knee again and and you know trust the physicality of the game >> after taking a hit like that and >> yeah after taking a hit like that? >> Uh I trust my knee a lot. Um I taking that hit it didn't really hurt. I was just laying there cuz I was a little tired. I'm not going to lie and I haven't played football in 8 months. So, you know, I'm still, you know, trying to get in that football shape. But, uh, I needed that. You know, it was a welcome to the NFL hit. You know, I needed it to break the ice. You know, I had I needed to get tal. You know, I need to, you know, have somebody to put a show on me, you know what I'm saying? So, it can, you know, make me get ready for the league. >> Tell us about the uh 18 yard catch and what it meant for you to get on the score score sheet like that. >> Oh, it meant it it was a it was a good catch. Uh I know uh I would have scored that, you know, I was just um thinking about that safety and I was trying to uh drop my shirt on the safety, but you know um you mean you mean give me some time when the season start. I'll be scoring many many of those. So yeah. >> What has been the key to returning before many thought you would? >> Um uh it really haven't been no key. Like I just been taking every day one day at a time, you know, uh taking it step by step, you know, uh trusting in what the trainers got planned for me and the strength staff and the coaches, you know, uh every day I come and work, you know what I'm saying? I put in the work and you know um at first the time the timeline was later, but um how I just work and kept improving, you know, um there was no reason to hold me back. So um um I was just trusting in God and just trusting in the plan that they had for me. >> The way you're going, how ready do you think you'll be in two weeks? Um, I'll be ready. Uh, I'm ready now, but I definitely would be ready in two weeks. Um, I really needed this game, you know, just to, you know, step out on the NFL field and play against some competition, you know, other than my, um, teammates in practice. Um, so I 100% will be ready. >> You told us, I think back when we first interviewed you that you have like a list of all the receivers that were preseason, you were kind of at the bottom like as your background or something. I'm curious, do you still have that as your background? And what I guess do you why why do you still have that if you still >> can you repeat again? >> Yeah. You said I think when we talked to you like after you first got drafted that you had a list of >> like curious you said that you still have that as your background and what sort of motivation you take away from >> um yeah of course I still have that um I still have that you know that list of all those receivers that you know got drafted before me. Um u I didn't know I was going to go that late. But it's all God's plans like I said and um it means a lot to me. You know, I always been the underdog. I always been the slept on guy. You know, it's just another opportunity in my life and another thing in my life that you know um I got to prove myself. So um I love that. You know, I love my back against the wall. You know, I love when God put, you know, a challenge in my life and you know, I know I'm always I come on the top because I know God got me. So yeah. talk about how you've built connections between Cam and some of the other quarterbacks in Miami's roster and then leading into today maybe some of the conversations you had with Cam on the sidelines in between drives. >> Uh you said how I build relationships with them. >> Yeah. >> Um you know just uh going throughout practice you know um and routes on there um trying to get the timing down and things like that. That's how you build you know relationship and that's how I've been building my relationship with my quarterback. Uh but on the sideline, you know, um me and Cam uh and the other quarterbacks in general, uh we all we all just, you know, uh you know, told each other what we saw and you know, if um he see this, then he going to throw it to me and things like that. So, uh I'm just really trusting him and trying to get open for him and um make a make a play for him, make a play for my team. So, yeah. >> To that point, today's action wasn't with Malik at quarterback. So, how big will building that chemistry, camaraderie be in the next two weeks? >> Say it again. How big will it be to build that chemistry, camaraderie with Malik Willis in the next two weeks as today's action was with him back then? >> Yeah, it'll be big. But um you know, it's it's just going to take time, you know, um and we got um I won't say we got time, but we do got time. Um you know, we uh now that I'm practicing, you know, full speed and things like that, we can build that chemistry and um I'm excited for it. So, yeah. >> How much earlier do you think you may have been drafted had the knee injury not been a factor? And is this comeback that you're on now. Um maybe giving you the last laugh on teams that passed over you. >> You said how early would I be? Would I did I think >> uh honestly I I was projected to go late first round um and or early second round. But um like I said, I'm always put God in. It was God's plan, you know. Um his plan was to not have me at the top, you know, too early, you know. And um I think uh well, I know cuz it's always been like that in my life. start from the bottom cuz you know where I'm from you know I always got it out the mud. So um you know I'm just happy to be you know a dolphin and um I'm ready you know to take on any challenges that you know um that comes in front of me and I know you know I'mma end up on top. >> Thank you Chris. He's yours. just I thought he did a great job. It was great to have him back out. He's been practicing for a little while now and you can just tell that he has that, you know, big playability and just to have him out there gives me a lot of comfort and confidence for sure. >> How did you feel you played today? >> I thought there was some good and some bad. Um, I felt like there were some missed opportunities that I had. Um, but I felt like I um stayed in there. I felt like I showed my toughness and my willingness to do whatever it takes to win and that's really what I what I what I wanted to show today and I felt like I did that. So, >> what's been the challenge uh for you running the the second, the third, whatever teams this preseason while you face guys who might start week one for your opponent or, you know, have been in the league for >> 8, nine, 10 years. Yeah, I think I think it's been a great challenge and knowing that some of their starters were going to be out there today. I think you can't really replicate that in practice. Even though you know you might go against the ones here, you can't simulate a game and being out there going against great competition only makes you better. It's going to make me mentally tough and the guys around me tougher. >> What do you think the next uh 48 hours will be like? start. >> I'm sure there's people that are, you know, anxious, but I know that the locker room put their best foot forward. I know every single one of those guys was in early, left late, and gave everything that they could to give themselves a chance, and now it's in God's hands. >> Do you think the biggest progress for you from last week starting to this week? I think just like confidence in myself, knowing that I can go out there and do it against the best and like I said, there were some good and some bad, but knowing that those good plays that I could build off that um for my next experience. So, >> what's the biggest uh area in which you think you've grown since you arrived here in South Florida? >> I think just my knowledge of the game. I think Bobby Sloick has done such a great job of teaching the quarterback's defense and running his system. I've been such a huge fan of him and the way that he's helped develop quarterbacks in the past and it's been so great to just learn the game of football from his from him and I think that's been some of the most improvement just seeing seeing the field a lot better than I did in the past. >> Thank you guys. Thank you. Thanks, man. How's the guys going? How you guys doing? >> How you doing? >> How would you evaluate uh I guess those last few drives that you got in the preseason? >> Yeah, I'm I'm just super grateful for the opportunity first off. Um you know, it's always a blessing to be out there playing with those guys. Um I felt like I left everything I could out there with those guys just battling. Um, you know, there's some opportunities that, um, we really had to take advantage of when we got that fumble in the red zone. We we got to turn that into points somehow. Um, but I'm just glad I gave it everything I had. Everyone that was out there, um, we're all competing for for spots on this team and, um, to just get an opportunity like that, it was great. >> What has been your experience of coming in undrafted, start off training camp, you get cut eventually, got to come back and uh, and get some game action here in the >> Yeah. Again, basically what I just said too is like I'm so grateful to to be back with these guys. Like I've built such great relationships with a lot of these guys in the team, especially a lot of these rookies. There's it's a such a big rookie class um this year and just building those relationships, building those relationships with the guys in the team. Um to get cut originally um it was really heartbreaking just because I know like I know a lot of these guys. I love playing with a lot of these guys. Like these coaches a lot. Um and to get an opportunity to come back play in these games, get two halves of football to play. Um, I mean, I can't I I'm just so thankful to get that get these opportunities and show what I got on tape. >> What was the biggest, I guess, point of progress for you individually from last week to this week? >> Um, I think it's just going out there just playing more free. Um, you know, being a quarterback, a lot is just being comfortable in the pocket, delivering from the pocket, um, but also taking chances downfield and we got the opportunities. We took I took a shot to, uh, uh, Terrence Marshall who made a great play today. took a shot to Jaylen Rager who um just a little bit of an overthrow there. But, you know, overall it was just great being out there with those guys and um I know just getting the more reps, more reps in practice, more reps in the games, you just started to feel more comfortable and you could play faster out there and play more free. >> You mentioned the pass to Marshall, I guess. What did you see on that that play? >> Yeah. Um I mean, Terence Marshall has been making plays left and right in um in practices. you give you give him a one-on-one ball, he he's he's coming down with it. And when he they gave him a one-on-one opportunity, the safety kicked, looked over to the field. Um he was one-on-one with that corner, so I wanted to give him an opportunity and um he came down with the play, which is awesome to see. >> What's something that you feel you'll need to continue to improve in order to make it? >> Yeah, I think the the biggest thing I I mean, I feel like I've showed my legs and I know that my athleticism is a big part of my game and um was a big part of my game in college as well. and just continuing to grow as a passer, having better pre- snap plans when you're going out there so you can almost start playing the game before the play even happens. Um, and just continue to deliver and and feel comfortable in the pocket and and and make plays that way. Um, once you get to that part of your game, then the defense is going to have a real trouble stopping you. When you have to use your when you can use your legs and throw from the pocket, like the team's going to have a lot of trouble. >> Awesome. Thank you guys. We got Trader up next and that's the last one. So, what was it like seeing Sua in opposing uniform? >> Uh, it was kind of weird, but it was bittersweet, too, cuz after the game, uh, we all came up to him, coraled him. Uh, that's our brother at the end of the day. Obviously, he's on another team. you got to compete against them. But after the final whistle blew, we all we all stampeded him and it was good to see my guy. >> Yeah, on that play especially um you know with that defense, you're going to need a lot of people to win their one-on-one matchups. um and a couple people did and you know just people tricking and getting off blocks was allowed us to get a free run um and just peppering every every runner on that plate especially and then defensively we went you know beginning of the week always have an emphasis to get three over running so this week we got three um I think it was three I believe um and that that helps the offense that gets moving gets field position creating turnovers you get points should be points especially where you get them at um and it creates juice as you see it bringing up the guys guys on the sideline getting everybody involved just just help the offense and defense get in the How does life change for for you guys now as we enter week zero and practice stops being about, you know, the install and getting guys up to speed and scouting each other and becomes more geared toward playing an actual opponent. >> Yeah, obviously you know with u you know rosters and stuff getting dwindled down. So, it's going to be a tough couple of days for a lot of people navigating that and just being there for our brothers and then switching up to like you said for for week one. Now, you know, the clock has started, now it's really on. Um preseason, you trying to figure out what you got and how to, you know, get in a rhythm and, you know, get the kinks and the rust off for everybody and just formulate, you know, a bond and connection, you know, through three games and couple of joint practices, but now it's really focused on, you know, the Raiders and getting ready to figure out how we scouting and game plan for them. So just switching that page of what do we need to do and how we need to go about things next week. >> Decent bit of action tonight. Is that something you really wanted after I guess you missed a little bit of a camp in the middle of it? >> Yeah, I mean not not playing uh for like it was a week or something like that. Like if I need to play I need to get, you know, on the field being able to go out there so I can feel good going into, you know, the real the real season. Getting to put my pads on people just filling the game out a little bit more. Um, I think I played a little less this game, but uh, it's good. You know, everybody wants to play. Everybody wants to, you know, be a part of something, and that's kind of like how I handled it. >> What did you learn about yourself coming back? >> You can do everything right. The prehab, preventatives, and have a great mindset off season and still life will hit you hard. You know, football game uh, the game of football is always unforgiving. You know what I mean? We're not promised nothing. We not guaranteed nothing. you know, I was doing everything I could to, you know, and that's kind of what I was kind of frustrated off when I got hurt. But, uh, that that shows to show like what we had to deal with and that's you got to chin up, chest up, you know what I mean? Um, you in a good position and then you get, hey, sit down. You got hurt. Now you got to do mental reps. Now you got to help other people. Now you got to figure out, okay, when I get back, try to be yourself. You know what I'm saying? So, it teaches a lot about yourself getting that callus and that resilience. You get resilience in different ways, but ultimately it makes you a better football player in some u instance. with new coaches and a new scheme. What's something that you learned about uh this defense throughout training camp and and preseason now that it's over? >> I feel like especially on on the field, it's a lot of X's on the field. Um you know, early off we get taught anybody can put in these places. We got a lot of vers uh versatile guys that's been moving around and different personnels and things like that. just being able to learn the system and play of one like that's just what helps our defense be uh aggressive and you know putting eyes on the quarterbacks getting eliminating space and checkdowns and everything like that. But this scheme's pretty good and you know, Coach Athlete does a great job and and Dugen of just preparing us and giving us how we're going to get attacked and we going over it every week. It just, you know, these are our strengths, these are our weaknesses and we got to figure out how to mitigate explosives, get TFLs, get sacks, get uh, you know, stop the run game and then ultimately limit the pass explosives. >> I know it was on the opposite side of the field, but I guess what was it like to see Chris Bell? >> Yeah, man. Uh, that guy is special. Think about it. Uh I used to watch that guy on the field like you know obviously when we have breaks or something just running routes. I'm like man he and he he was just hurt. Um but he looks good man and it's good to see my guy out there. I know you know a lot of people that's been in that position. You don't get to play for a long long time and then especially draft of where he was and the and the pressure and the hype that he had just to go out there and get that feeling get get a hit like get tackled. I talked to him after this joking with him. I was like how it feel to get hit again. He's like oh man it's good to get back out there. But it's good to see our guys back out there and you know that's what it's all about especially camp seeing guys go back out there and you know have fun you know again like I was saying about his story getting having an injury and having to come back at the end of camp. So um we're excited to see where he's about to go. >> Can't remember if we've asked him but is being a captain something you would like to do even as a second year player? >> Yeah I anybody wants to be a captain? Um, but it's I feel like being a captain is kind of something you choose. You know what I mean? Before you're actually chosen to be one. You know what I'm saying? You don't just, hey, I want to be leader. Like, you got to have the actions. You got to back it up with the work ethic, the plays, and just being able to corral the guys. Like, regardless if I'm a captain or not, you're going to hear hear me like my voice hurts right now. I'm yelling. I'm running down on the sidelines helping people when I can. Um, and just, you know, and even this week too, like guys are asking me about, you know, the 53 or the 90, what are they looking for, what to do, and I'm just trying to help everybody, you know what I mean? Um, like I said, but regardless of Catherine or not, how many years it takes me to be one, I'm going to be myself. I'm going help everybody. I'm going try to strain for this team, and that's what I'm going to do. Be me.

title: Is the Dolphins' Best Receiver Being Rushed Back?
text: He said something along the lines of you know, they've they've encouraged me to make sure that I listen to my body and be honest with them. >> Yes. >> Then he also said I'm I've got to push myself and work through scar tissue and things of that nature. And yes, that's everybody's mindset when they're coming back from an injury. Can they trust the knee? Can Can they favor it? Can they play through soreness? But I have do and Pooh Part goes much longer than me. And Pooh Part actually covered the NFL when the day was your your you suffered an ACL injury, your career was done. Like Um cuz there was a day where ACL injury it was over for you. I mean, there's so many different stats. You can look at EPA and successful run percentage, but the Jets were a pretty good running team last year. It's like the only thing they did well, I think. So, uh yes, I do believe they could be a top-10 rushing offense, for sure. >> And that was with Fields and that was with I'm sorry, Jet. That was with Fields, you know, cranking out some yards, too. So, you know, you take him out and then you would think That's why I say more like 12, maybe a little bit of a step back, but still good, still solid. title: Saints-Cowboys Preseason Recap on the Saints Podcast | Aug. 28, 2026
text: Welcome to the New Orleans Saints podcast training camp 2026 presented by Rouses Markets. Here from players, coaches, and get analysis from our team of broadcasters as we break down preseason games and practice. That's right. We're talking about practice, baby. The New Orleans Saints podcast starts right now. Here are your hosts, John DeShazer and Todd Graffagnini. >> And it is the New Orleans Saints podcast live field level actually on the field here at AT&T Stadium. Jerry World in Arlington, Texas as the Saints have picked up their first and only preseason win because there's no more preseason games. Regular season is up next in 2 weeks, but the Saints close out the preseason with a 27 to 24 win over the Dallas Cowboys. Todd Graffagnini and John DeShazer with you here in Arlington. JD, first things first, there's I mean, there's a lot to unpack tonight, but it was look, preseason or not, really good to get a win. I thought the Saints played really solid football wiping away the bad taste that we had uh last week in LA. Uh I just thought it was a good night all around. And of course, Daniel Carlson, who was literally signed this week, wins the game with a 53-yarder just at the 2-minute mark. Clutch kick. Saints have to hold on, play some defense, which they do, and they win the game. Just a real positive way to end the preseason. >> Yeah, I would I would say solid overall, but I thought the I thought the first half might have been out borderline borderline outstanding. Um 17-9 halftime lead, I think it was, but I think the offense was pretty clean with Spencer Rattler. Rattler was eight of 10 from, you know, eight of 10 passing in that in that first half, 79 yards, and he ran for a touchdown. Uh two yard two carries, nine yards, and a touchdown. I thought the offense was really clean in that first half operationally. Only only committed three five um three penalties in the first half, and one of those was defensive. So, two on offense. Now, two of those happened both of those happened on that first drive. I just thought they were really good on offense in the first half. And and so, that was great to see after not scoring against the Rams in a 34-nothing loss. But, yeah, I I I you know, it's a good way to finish off the preseason. Now, you want to get on into the regular season, but just to get that taste out of your mouth, because even though it's preseason, you don't want to sleep on a 34-nothing loss. Even though it's preseason, you don't want to have that kind of result. And look, I I think Kellen Moore was ticked off after that game, and and his team came out and played a much much better version. >> Look, it starts on the first drive. And, you know, give credit to the Saints. Crop right a very good uh kick return to start the game. And then, Spencer Rattler, who he had something to prove. You know, you could have said, is the number two quarterback battle still up for grabs? Well, I think that battle ended tonight. Even though Zach Wilson accounted for himself nicely, Spencer Rattler, the way that he played in the first half, I think established himself solidly as the number two. But, man oh man, it was fun to watch that team uh really mix it up, especially on the ground, John. Uh the Saints were outstanding in the first half, uh running for 115 yards in the first half, 6.8 per carry. Uh Kendre Miller returned back to where he went to college. Remember, he went to college just up the road in Fort Worth at TCU. Well, he ran angry tonight and just had a really solid first half. And look, I just love the way the Saints were able to run the ball tonight. >> Yeah, if you run it 32 times for 169 yards and three touchdowns, probably going to win that game. Look, I understand a lot of people look at this game and say, "Okay, they were playing second team as third team and they were playing against, you know, plumbers and barbers and, you know, all those kinds of names you want to call guys that you don't think might make a team." But still, you have to go out and execute. You're still got to do it. And look, they were playing against, if you want to call it that, theoretically the same guys against the Rams and didn't get it done. So, you always want to see a team get it done. Now, I understand Dallas had a bad defense last year, even the starters. But certainly, if you're the Saints, you want to come out, you establish that run game, and that pretty much kept the Cowboys on their heels in this game. You get C.J. Donaldson to add in something. You get Adrian Estime four carries, 46 yards. So, the Saints had great production in the run game. And sometimes when you have that kind of production in the run game, it's because the quarterback might break out with a scramble for 30, 40 yards or something like that. That was not the case in this one. The Saints got up and they bullied and they pushed and they created those seams for their running backs and they were able to take great advantage of it in this game. And that's exactly what you want to see in a game like this. >> Was the defense perfect? No, but the key was early in the game they held Dallas to field goals. And of course, Dallas has one of the best field goal kickers in the league in Brandon Aubrey, who makes a 55-yarder look like an extra point, and I'm not exaggerating. He had a rare, and I mean rare, miss from 57 yards in the first half. But to the Saints' credit, they were able to take that short field and get one of their two touchdowns on that Spencer Rattler 8-yard run after the long run by Audric Estime. So, you took advantage of a miss. Bend, but don't break. Give field goals. Now, the Cowboys were able to come back, score 15 points in the fourth quarter as Sam Howell, their quarterback, was able to engineer a couple of drives, tied it up at 24, but then the big drive at the end. And you got to you got to credit Zach Wilson. That play he made on first down, which was going to be a sack and a loss of at least 10 yards. And if that is a sack, the Saints do not win this game. I'm just telling you that right now. He improvised, somehow got it to C.J. Donaldson, who got the first down, and then you were off and running. And of course, Carlson with the clutch kick at the end. >> And look, 10-15 years ago, that might be an in the grasp. And what benefits Zach Wilson is he's a mobile quarterback. So, the quarter So, the So, the the officials give him the benefit of the doubt. They say, "Okay, he might have been able to get out of that." And fortunately for the Saints, he was able to spin out just enough to throw that little flip pass to C.J. Donaldson, who ran 13 yards with it and got the first down. Again, an impressive close by the Saints. You win games by holding high-powered offenses to field goals. Yep. Technically right now, he's over They got He was drafted by New England. Bolden, Avery Thomas, Dejean Well, he's really not a corner anymore. Rick Lovato is way over it. Quinyon is technically over it. Ringo is 6 ft or over it. That's I don't know if there's another team with corners that tall. But unfortunately, Mike, some of these guys won't be playing very much for them in the fall. >> Uh last one before we get you out of here. Um Ty Robinson was interesting cuz he's obviously flashed and Fangio said on Tuesday, well, you got to do it against better competition. Um is he a guy that we keep an eye on tonight or does he really just have no uh ability to kind of crack, you know, a rotational spot here with the depth? >> He won't play even if he makes it, Mike. Vic only plays four D-tackles unless one or two things happen. Injury or like if for some reason, there's no way to know this and it probably won't happen. Byron Young's been a great waiver claim for the Eagles. If he got hurt or was playing poorly, sure, Robinson, if he makes it and I have him right now I right now I have him on the roster. Um the good thing about his tape, Mike, his tape was so good, I was told. I expect the Eagles to get some interest in him. I I really do. Another team told me uh he said, "Look, you go he And this guy was clearly aware and I he was aware of the quote that Vic gave to us." In New England when he said his he was on life support. Not not really. That was really not nice but very funny. I I Mike, when >> Talk about Robinson, his chances, yeah. >> Yeah, when when his chances he he said on life support. I looked at other reporters like, "Did he really say that?" I guess he did. Never a at a loss for words and he's a truth-teller, but boy, did Robinson look really good. And look, it's you know, what it is. >> three tackles for loss, I mean, that's some production there. >> And Eagles are super deep. Zion Wilson shown the undrafted free agent, he's shown up. Gabe Hall's been a good story, but he's more of a tweener. And then of course, you got You are Bernard, Mike. There it was It's very rare to have good depth at D-tackle. The Eagles are one of those rare teams. >> Yep, and uh obviously uh this is the last chance for some of these guys to make the roster to flash tonight. You can listen to the game with Merrill Reese and Mike Quick right here on 97.3 ESPN. We got Football at Four Monday to break it all down and we will be into regular season mode. Check out the Inside the Birds podcast on all podcasting platforms. Adam Caplan, we'll catch up with you next week, man. >> Sounds good. Thank you. >> Adam Caplan everybody from the Inside the Birds podcast. Don't forget Football at Four is back for another season. Mosher is here on For a Mosher Monday. title: Football at Four: Some Younger Eagles Who Could Make an Impact
text: Football 4 powered by the Inside the Birds podcast, which you can get on all podcasting platforms. We got preseason football tomorrow night. It's the final one before the real thing happens. We got one more test run. >> [music] >> Football 4 powered by the Inside the Birds podcast is brought to you by Fanatic Sportsbook at Ocean Casino Resort in Atlantic City. We're back there every Monday. And of course, Andrew Di Cecco's here every Thursday. We got a lot to dive into. Two preseason games down, one joint practice, and now a final preseason. Let's take a look at Andrew's overview of what we've seen as training camp has come to a close for 2026. Andrew, what's up, my man? >> Hey, Mike. Don't well. Good to be with you. >> Yeah, man. It's been a little while. Missed you the last couple of weeks, but that means we're getting closer to the season. And a lot of stuff happening. Uh obviously, camp comes to a close here. Um tomorrow night will be the last preseason tilt. Give me a couple of guys as a lot of people always like, "Hey, I want to hear the guys Andrew's looking at." Who are some guys you're keeping an eye on for tomorrow that this game might be important for? >> Offensive lineman Jake Majors. He's cross-trained at center and guard. Well, he's a center by trade out of University of Texas. Was on the Eagles practice squad all last season. I think he's really made some strides, Mike, in training camp. Tough player. Set a Texas record with 56 starts. And that says a lot. But I think he's done a nice job at guard as well. Now, the reason why you need to keep an eye on him is because there is some questions as to how that number 10th that number 10 offensive line spot might shake out. You have Michael Morris, the draft pick. You have Jake Majors. You have John Ajuku, who's done some good things in training camp as well. But I I I think that Majors has done a nice job over the last 2 weeks. and we'll see what he's able to do in the finale. I would also say on the defensive side K'Von Wallace is an undrafted free agent. Everyone talks about Maximus Poole, but in my view I think Gushiken having watched him for 17 practices now has been the more impressive player. Now both to be clear are not I don't want to say long shots, but it's unlikely given the way that the roster is shaping up, but I think Gushiken because he can play nickelback and safety and he's been working in a little bit more over the last week or so. He's an interesting player if for no other reason than maybe a practice squad slot and maybe elevate him at some point on game day. And then I'm going to look at Cameron Latu, the tight end fullback. I've been on Cameron Latu since last summer when Jihad Campbell was just a heat-seeking missile coming downhill. All the tight ends struggled to contain him Mike, but not Cameron Latu. There was a couple of plays in one practice where he stonewalled him. I wrote down number 87 in my notes and I kept an eye on him throughout the rest of the preseason, made some plays on special teams. I think he is just a tenacious player, a really physical blocker and to this day I'm puzzled how the Eagles didn't use him more last season, but I think he's an interesting player as they start to whittle the roster down to 53. >> Uh Andrew, what does that mean for Eli Shorter? We have not been hearing very good things about him so far. Do you have the same takeaways from his camp the second round pick? Uh do you see a little very little impact so far and moving into the season? >> Well it has been underwhelming to be clear, but I also like to re-emphasize that progress is not linear. Everybody progresses at different rates. Now when the Eagles drafted Eli Shorter it was that should have been widely expected that he was a developmental prospect and sometimes those things take time and I think Sean Mannion, the Eagles offensive coordinator, outlined it well. Everyone thinks that you can just plug and play, and there's not going to be growing pains, but he abilities being a tight end at this level. You have the blocking component, the receiving component, the alignment, and all these different things that he's being asked to do that is going to be foreign to him relative to what he's accustomed to at Vanderbilt. So, it's going to take some time. Now, that's not to say that the tight end position isn't a big question mark, because I do have quite a few questions, but in terms of Eli Stowe, just relax a little bit. That That would be my That would be my uh my cautionary uh you know, message out there, because it seems like there's a lot of angst about him, and I think young players deserve an opportunity to grow and develop, and the Eagles prioritize player development, and this is going to be uh a tall task here for Ryan McHugh, the new tight ends coach, because Jason Michael has had an extensive track record of doing so, and they're going to have to They deserve the benefit of the doubt. >> Uh Andrew, our poll question today has to do with the receivers. Outside of DeVonta Smith, which guy uh do you think will have the biggest impact of the other group of receivers? >> Don Tavion Wicks. I I really like what I've seen from him in training camp from beginning of camp to the end. You could see the rapport between Wicks and Jalen Hurts really budding throughout the summer. Now, he's not someone that's going to take the top off of the defense. He's really effective in the short to intermediate levels of the field, a really good separator at the top of his routes, and I haven't seen him drop many passes, if any, in training camp to my recollection, which is something that has been sort of a a mark on him. He has struggled with drops in his career, but I think he's really establishing that trust with Hurts, and he's going to be someone who I think will will see a decent amount of volume, and he's a big question mark, understandably, because he's never exceeded more than 39 receptions in a season, never had more than 74 or 75 targets in a given year. But from what I've seen this season, this training camp, I think he's going to be someone that they that can be depended upon and he's going to be an effective chain mover for them. >> Um you've seen Lemon for a couple days now. I know he missed a lot of time. Are you hopeful that he can have uh some sort of impact in this offense? >> Well, it's been pretty clear going back to the public practice, Mike, that the Eagles are going to find a way to get the ball into the hands of Britain Covey, Lemon. Whether that's manufacturing touches or intermediate throws that really accentuate what he can do as a route runner. And I would also temper expectations because there's going to be growing pains here. He missed a lot of time this summer. That's not that that shouldn't generate any angst. He's back on the practice field. He was working after practice on the final training camp day with Sean Mannion. So he he's really taking, you know, he he mentioned the other day about being more professional. And then there's a lot of ways you can interpret that. I have to think that it has a lot to do with just how to approach an injury, the recovery process, and things like that. But he is someone that I think don't have to necessarily squint to see him being able to make an early impact. And I would just temper expectations because there are players who are further ahead of him in terms of knowledge of this offense. But he's a first-round pick. They're going to find a way to get And another area to keep an eye on would be Britain Covey, Lemon potentially as a punt returner. He's worked there when he has been on the practice field. He was one of the four players repping there final day of practice along with Britain Covey, Cooper DeJean, and I believe Quez Watkins. So of those players, I mean Cooper DeJean's not going to do it. Quez Watkins and Britain Covey in all likelihood aren't going to be on the roster. And so I think Britain Covey, Lemon has a good bet to to at least see that. And I would like to see him get a couple reps if he does in fact play on Friday. >> Yeah, and obviously a lot of expectations for Lemon. And they've got Hollywood Brown here. What about Darius Cooper? Is he a guy, too, that could, you know, I asked the question because I'm looking at the Green Bay offense the last couple of years and they've had just had a like four or five guys, you know, one guy has 700 yards, another guy has 600. I would imagine DeVonta Smith is probably the main guy, but is there enough in this offense for three, four wide receivers? That typically has not been the case here. >> Right, and it's important to remember that they're going to in all likelihood spread the football around in this West Coast offense, and it is a true West Coast offense, but it's going to run through DeVonta Smith, Dallas Goedert, Saquon Barkley, I believe is going to have a larger role in the passing game. You have Dontayvion Wicks, so and you have McKay Lemon. So, I don't I don't I always like to you know, temper expectations there with Darius Cooper. What we saw this summer is real. He's a He's a big-time contributor in the in training camps and he was involved in the offense, but you also have to keep in mind the offense that they're in. They're not a pass-centric team. They are a low-volume passing attack and it's going to be all about the running game, Saquon Barkley and the Eagles offensive line and others in the passing game, which I mentioned, it's going to funnel through them first and foremost. >> All right, Andrew, check out Football at Four tomorrow night. The Eagles take on the Bengals in the last preseason tilt there. You mentioned some things on the offensive side. Obviously, the defense could be a very, very good this year. I want to get your thoughts on the last couple of years. I thought the question to Fangio yesterday when asked about Jalen Hurts, like how good could he be? Is this what you expected? My question is more are we ready to see Jalen Hurts be the guy on this defense in terms of pass rush? >> You know, I I think I think he's close. I think he just might be there, Mike. What What I've seen from Jalen Hurts is a player who went from 241 snaps as a rookie, 693 last season, where he led all Eagles pass rushers in snaps, sacks with 6 and 1/2, led the team in interceptions, and led the edge rushers in quarterback hits, which I believe was 24. So, every year he's taken well, the first 2 years he's taken a big step forward from year 1 to year 2. And this summer, there hasn't been a day that's gone by where I haven't written down number 58 and number 97 in my notes. He has been a uh an absolute force off the edge, but he's also an effective two-way player now. He's filled out his frame, and I say this a lot, but a lot was made about his athleticism, and it was widely expected that he was going to be a work in progress and take a little bit of time to develop, but I think the the technical aspect of the game has now caught up to the athleticism, and he's able to play freely. He has a better idea of how to combat tackles and counter moves, and has a much deeper arsenal of pass rush moves from which to to choose from. So, I think he is ready to to take that next step this year. That's something that I actually asked Vic Fangio about in the spring, and he pretty much said he gave a great answer, but he pretty much said he just needs to keep doing what he's doing. So, I I think the sky's the limit for him, and I think the Eagles are well equipped to handle the the absence, should there be an absence, for of Jonathan Gannon from, you know, in week 1 or whatever the case is, with Ja'Wuan Johnson, but also Nolan Smith has quietly had a nice training camp as well. He's healthy, he's extremely violent and physical off the edge, and I think he's gotten a lot of pressures, and he's also filled out his frame a little bit more as well. >> All right. Uh you wrote about Ty Robinson over at insidethebirds.com, and yesterday Vic Fangio was asked about him on a couple different questions regarding him. This guy was a fourth-round pick, and I think he's way down the depth chart here, but one of the things that Fangio said like, "Well, you got to do it against better players. You don't get that opportunity." So, no matter what Robinson does tomorrow night, do you see him having any role on this team? >> Yeah, well, you you got to earn those opportunities, right? Byron Young has earned those opportunities. So, for example, whenever whether it's Jalen Carter, Jordan Davis, Moro Ojemo, whatever they needed a spell, Byron Young was the first guy up there because he's proven it. It's hard to do it when you don't get those opportunities, but you know, you have to earn those. And what I will tell you about Ty Robinson is that it seems around the midway point of training camp, he got off to a slow start. And I don't know if it had any coincidence, but right around the time where he got into a little dust-up with Tyler Steen, it almost awakened a sort of confidence in him where he was approaching things differently. He talked about Clint Hurtt and then the exit meetings and emphasizing to him to really refine and and grow in terms of mobility and flexibility to eliminate some stiffness and not being lopsided. And that's something that I think is really been reflected in his reps. When you're watching him play now, you're seeing someone who has a little bit more wiggle to him and isn't as stiff of an athlete. The strength has never been a question. It's about the other elements of that game that you need to be an effective player. And for right now, he's done all the right things. It's going to be on him to make sure that he stays on schedule. And if he's able to do that and earn the trust of Vic Fangio, and that is sort of stems from consistent and he will be able to to carve out a few more snaps than he did last season. >> Uh Epps and Michael Carter, and he says it's close, it's close. Michael's been doing a good job back there. Uh what is the battle that those two guys right now are you know, where do you see Epps and Carter? >> Yeah, what's interesting about Vic Fangio and and and playing safety in his defense is that I don't know that you need to be a superstar. You need to be someone who is fundamentally sound, highly intelligent, and there's not going to be a high variance nature to your game. And that's Marcus Epps. He's not going to make the big play, but he's often going to be in the right position to make those tackles, make those plays, smart football player. But for all that, and that's great, I think Michael Carter's had a better training camp. But I think that what maybe works against Michael Carter here, through no fault of his own, is that he wears three different hats. He can play safety, he can play nickel back, of course, and he's their dime defensive back as well. So I think Vic Fangio, if you listen to his answer and you're able to kind of sift through it, you could tell that he's really enamored with his versatility, and that may prove to be too valuable. But Carter had three interceptions in training camp, he's rangier, he has really good short area quickness, he sees things quickly, and I like his eye discipline. I was a big fan of the player watching him with the New York Jets, and he has a lot of a lot of his skills and tools from nickel back that have translated to the safety position, but he's still new to it, and I think there is a comfort level there with someone like Marcus Epps. So I do believe that it will be Marcus Epps week one at safety when the Eagles are in their nickel package. >> Now you asked about Andre Sam yesterday, I think that was you anyway. Did Is he in the mix at all? >> You know, Andre's had a really good camp, and I thought he had a really good two practices there in New England. He was really physical. There's something to be said for a player, and Vic Fangio does not throw away practice reps. He's not going to put you out there and if he believes that you're going to mess things up. Andre's seen a ton of reps, all with the second team, very sporadically with the first team, and I I I think right now, he's 27 years old. It's hard for me to envision the Eagles feeling the need to keep him, knowing that they've waived him for two years now. He's made it to the practice squad. He just seems to be a very dependable practice player who they can elevate on game day, and I think they're really comfortable there. But if you listen to what Vic Fangio said, he called him reliable and trustworthy, which that was my read throughout the summer and really last year, but I don't know that it's hard for me to envision them keeping Andre Sam or even Gushiken or Maximus Pulli, just given the way the roster structured right now. >> All right, he was asked about the defensive backs yesterday, the cornerback depth right now, and he, you know, he said, "I feel good about Quinyon and Rick." And of course uh Jones has been hurt. I think he's back there now, but >> He said He said you Rick? >> Rick Woolen, yep. Uh so Q, Rick Woolen, Jonathan Jones, he he mentioned but he said he missed a lot of time. Uh do you think he feels comfortable with that room right now? >> Well, it's hard to imagine that he does, but this is the group that they're working with right now, Mike, and you can argue that they have, and it would be a compelling argument that the Eagles have that the top three cornerback group. I mean, I'm throwing Cooper DeJean in there at as the nickel back. But beyond that, there's a lot of questions. Jonathan Jones last practice on I believe August 8th. Now, he is a veteran, he's going to be 33 in September. That's 33 in NFL years. But is that someone that you can rely on to get through a full season, or is that sort of a precursor of what might come? Might what might follow? Um Mac McWilliams is someone that he's had some positive moments. They haven't been consistent moments. He hasn't been able to sustain that. There's been practices where he's showing signs of encouragement, and then there's been some opportunities that I'm sure he'd like to have back. But he is someone who can play nickel back, and he can play outside. So you like that there. He was a draft pick last year, so that does count for something. And Kelee Ringo is a player that is a tremendous special teamer, but he's at best a fifth corner. I don't think that Vic Fangio under any circumstances would want to put him out there, but I do get the sense that Vic likes him a little bit. He's gone out of his way to prop him up and and commend him on some of the things that he's done. There has been some positive moments in camp, not not enough, but I think he's pretty safe, especially when they released safety JT Gray, who's a three-time All-Pro and one of the NFL's best gunners for a number of years now. When you release someone like that, well, I think Ringo's your gunner and going to be your core special teamer. >> Yeah. All right, uh good stuff. Uh who's your backup quarterback? >> If I'm making the call, it's Andy Dalton. I I I think there's a lot of value of having someone who has experience in this system. He's entering his 16th season right now. He can be an effective sounding board for Jalen Hurts. And I don't know that there's been a big enough discrepancy between Andy Dalton and Tanner McKee this summer to sway it one way or the other. I would default to the veteran and give you that stability there. I'm I'm also not as high on Tanner McKee as um it seems like many are, but that that's kind of where I'm at with it. >> All right, Andrew DiCecco. By the way, you an Alice Cooper guy at all? >> Yeah, I like Alice Cooper. I saw him open for him and his band, which is which was outstanding, open for Mötley Crüe in about 2015. When that was supposed to be the final tour for Mötley Crüe. I have that poster. They're still touring right now, Mike. Explain that to me. >> I don't know, man, but Cooper's playing Halloween night in Atlantic City. I don't know. Alice Cooper Halloween could get some get get a little kooky at that show, don't you think? We >> Yeah, that's that's something I I I might entertain if it if it works with my schedule. >> All right, we'll have to take a look. October 31st, Halloween night, Alice Cooper. We might have to do that show. I know we're trying to find I got to find something for us to go to here before before it gets too late here. All right, man. We'll we'll talk next time we talk we'll be getting ready for the Washington Commanders. It'll be fun. Thanks, bud. >> I'm going to hold you I'm going to hold you to that, Mike, and I will talk to you next week. >> Take care, man.

title: Jack Pyburn on Focusing on His Process | Press Conference | Tampa Bay Buccaneers
text: Yeah, I mean like I I mean I've said it over and over, it's about my process. You know, I'm not outcome-based anymore and I wasn't in college and that, you know, can get you in bad mental spaces. So, you just have to work the same way every single day. You have to prepare the same way whether it's an off day, um whether it's a work day, you know, approach it with intentionality and that's what I've done every single day to become a better player and understand my game and just develop as a pass rusher. You know, I've poured my life into this and just trying to show that I'm more than just a run stopper. You know, I'm tired of hearing that. >> Not the ideal performance tonight by the team, but what can you say about the defensive effort against the stops on fourth down and obviously the pass rush? >> Yeah, man, I we played really hard as a defense. Um you know, I I feel like we could have helped our offense out a little bit more in some situations, but overall I feel like we played really hard. Um and that's something you can improve on. You know, you can't coach effort and I feel like our defense showed tremendous effort and, you know, we executed at a at a at a pretty high level for the most part and, you know, we just got to continue to get better. >> Sorry if you're asked this already, Jack, but do you feel like you played well enough here in the preseason to get a roster spot? >> That's up to them. That's up to the front office, you know, I just like I said, I just show up every day and try to put my best foot forward and that's all you can do. >> How are you going to spend the next two days? >> How am I going to spend the next two days? Uh I'm going to go home. I'm going to sleep. I'm going to eat some food tomorrow and lay by the pool and, you know, I chill out, go to the facility, get some rehab and yeah, that's about it and then Sunday I'll figure it out. >> I know that this week has been crazy with with the college with the lawsuit and and everything. Have you been following that? I mean I know obviously that's another option that you've talked about pursuing and how has that been kind of playing in your mind here this week? >> Like I said, dude, I I've literally only been focused on making this team and playing football. You know, it's not other people outside of this are handling that and I've just been trying to play football. You know, that's been my main concern. You know, I don't I'm not on social medias. I don't see it. I don't care about it. I'm literally just trying to play football. That's all I'm trying to do. >> All right, thanks, Jack. >> Thanks, Jack. >> Appreciate y'all. >> Appreciate it.

title: Todd Bowles on Preseason Finale vs. Jacksonville | Press Conference | Tampa Bay Buccaneers
text: Hey coach, first your decision to uh you know, to start Jaylen and play him into the third quarter. >> We definitely want to see more of him. Want him to get some more experience. Want him to play against the uh the twos as opposed to the threes and fours and getting them in there and see how he operated. So, we wanted to give him a long lengthy look. >> Has he shown you enough to be the number two quarterback on this team? >> Uh he's shown a lot. He's shown a lot. We're going to go back and evaluate the film. It's not really the completions. It's the overall operation uh to make sure we're fine with that. And then we'll come back and look at the film because it you know, it wasn't very good offensively tonight. >> What's your reaction to the overall performance of the team tonight? >> Not good enough. Anytime you get shut out, you know, I I didn't think we protected the quarterback enough. We couldn't run the ball. Uh we gave up a special teams touchdown. Uh defense fought. They had some mistakes, but at least they fought. Um I thought two out of the three phases didn't show up. >> Uh we saw Keontay Scott get a little banged up. Any update on him or what injury he has? >> Not yet. I think it's an ankle. I'll wait and see. >> How about Mo Kamara? Mo Kamara injury? >> Uh I think it's a knee, but I'll wait and see what it is to what depth. >> Now, Benjamin Morrison made a a nice play there breaking up the touchdown. Um for him to battle through his injury and the get some game reps here, how how happy are you with what you've seen out of him as you turn to the regular season? >> Man, I'll watch the tape. It's just good to see him play a half, you know. He hadn't been out there for him to come out there and play a half and play all the special teams. Uh shows that he's finally healthy. So, he's just got to get the time on task now and get the get the reps in. >> You mean? In a game like this, guys are fighting for the last roster spots. Do you think that guys like Aiden Gardens and Jack Pyburn maybe helped themselves out a little bit tonight? >> Uh I got to look at the tape. Obviously, uh I know Pyburn had one one or two sacks. I'm sure he had two sacks again, but I got to look at the totality of it. That's a deep position as well. Garns has been playing consistent the last few weeks, so you know, we got some tough decisions to make. >> Seemed like there were a few special teams mishaps, including that return. What was your evaluation of the special teams play this whole game? >> Obviously, you give up a touchdown, it's not very good. They made some plays in the first half. I think they got worn down a little bit playing offense and defense and playing special teams in the second half, but it's kind of what it takes in this league to make this team. >> Are there any positions that you might think are the the most difficult to make a decision on with these roster cuts coming? >> I mean, they're all difficult. You know, you get to know these guys and be around them all. It doesn't matter the position. It is it's hard to tell people that they're they're not going to be on the team anymore. >> Do you have any concerns about the depth of your offensive line? I know you you like your first five guys and maybe kind of swing tackle. >> I like the first five and when everybody's healthy, I'll look at the tape. If you judge by the night, yeah, there's concern of it, but I'll look at the totality of the tape and see where it came from. >> Anything else? >> Okay, thank you. Thanks so much. Appreciate it.

title: Jalon Daniels on His Performance Throughout Preseason | Press Conference | Tampa Bay Buccaneers
text: It's good, y'all. >> Jalen, how would [clears throat] you evaluate your performance tonight? >> Um a lot of miscues, a lot of things that, you know, we definitely could have done better offensively. Um obviously, you know, when you go up there and you don't score any points, that's that's nothing that you, you know, you don't really want, especially as a quarterback. And um obviously, we haven't watched the film yet, but I think I do think that there was uh some good things that we did on film as well. And um obviously, there was some things that we need to clean up. So, we're going to go go ahead, look at the film, and get better from there. >> What did you learn at all from there? How about the entire postseason or preseason in training camp? Confident in >> Yeah, I mean, um as I've continued to tell y'all since since getting here, um I have God on my side, and I truly believe that, you know, everything that that I've been able to do up to this point is has been because of him. So, um I'm not going to lose faith. I'm I'm going to keep my faith in God, and at the end of the day, everything is going to happen Everything that happens happens for a reason, and um I'm going to let God handle those decisions. >> When did you learn When did you learn that you were going to start this game and play into the third quarter? And do you feel like that was a, you know, because of what you did the first two games, an opportunity to maybe become the the backup to Baker Mayfield? >> Yeah, I mean, you know, I'm someone who always says, "Whenever your number's called, you got to be able to You got to [clears throat] be ready to go out there and play football." Uh so, whenever they told me uh today that I was going to be able to go out there and start, I was like, "All right, bet. Let's go out there and play some football." Like, I've been Like I keep telling y'all, I've been playing this game since I was a kid. So, being able to get those extra reps, being able to to go out there and be the first quarterback out there, obviously, that's that's a dream come true. You know, being able to start a a NFL game as a starting quarterback, that's something that that you always dream of. So, uh obviously, grateful for the opportunity. Um and, you know, like I said, we got to get better from there. >> How tough was it though because the protection wasn't good? You had some drop passes on third down. How hard was it to get things going? >> Uh obviously, we never we never caught a rhythm tonight. And when you're not able to catch a rhythm offensively, uh it's kind of hard to be able to keep keep moving the sticks. And um I think that that's the big reason why we weren't able to to score points today. When you're not able to continue to keep moving the sticks, um, that's something that's not going to be able to go good. And as a quarterback, you know, I I take all of that on the chin. As soon as we're not able to keep moving those sticks, I take all of that on I take all the blame for that. >> Not the outcome that you wanted tonight, but is this a learning lesson in terms of you can't get too high with some of the big performances or too low with tonight? >> Yeah, yeah, absolutely. Um, my my sister's always telling me you'll you'll never be as good as they say you are and you'll never be as bad as they say you are. So, I I go into every single every single rep that I get even uh, even kill, uh, very level-headed, you know, never want to want to get too too confident, but you also don't want to lose confidence cuz in this game, if you lose confidence in yourself, you're not going to be able to go out there and perform. So, um, I'm always remain confident in my abilities, remain confident in being able to to run this system and um, like I keep saying, we're going to get better. >> How do you feel about your preseason as a whole? >> Um, I think that there's definitely some good in there, but obviously, like I keep telling y'all, I'm someone who I believe I'm my worst critic. And uh, as much as people want to say that there's good in there, I always look at the bad. Look at all the miss the miss passes, the miss pre-snap checks. I mean, we had a fumble today and I that's 100% on me. I have to be able to communicate better and um, the when you're looking at those little things, you want to be able to grow from it. >> This guy was signed after the draft. Do you get any special kick out of seeing guys like Aidan Gardens and Jack Pyburn succeeding? >> Absolutely. Yeah, no, absolutely. I mean, um, to be able to see a a UDFA go out there and make plays, that's something you love to see because, you know, they go out there with that chip on their shoulder. And I've been able to see AG be able to perform literally since rookie mini camp. Jack Pyburn has been someone who's continued to make plays day in and day out. Like he's told y'all about his work ethic and how much he does on a day-to-day basis, being one of the first guys in the building and being able to do as much as he can to prepare himself to go out there and play football. >> I know you're a confident player and I know you've been playing been in a long time, but um, does does this your preseason and what you've done kind of confirm to you that look, I should have been drafted. I know that that you know, all that stuff that happened you know, that that you're going to be a good player in this league? >> Um, like I keep saying, my journey's my journey. God put me in this position for a reason. And um, something my mom told me at after the draft was, I don't know why you're in this position, but at the end of the day it's happening to you for a reason. And I think that God gives his toughest battles to his strongest soldiers. So, um, if I'm in a position where I have to be able to show others that this mountain can be moved, then that's exactly what I'm going to do. I'm going to go out there and um, do everything that I can to be able to go out there and make plays. So, um, draft pick, UDFA, doesn't matter. I got the opportunity to be able to come out here and play NFL football. So, I'm forever grateful for that. >> Appreciate y'all watching. Appreciate it.

title: Todd Bowles Reviews Bucs vs. Jaguars | Press Conference Live Stream
text: question will come from Greg Almond. >> Hey Todd, I hope you're doing a little getting back home. So, that'll have a lot to do with whether we keep the extra one or not and how healthy these guys are going forward. Greg Almond, >> I know you addressed this a little bit last night, but just just want to ask you the overall uh offensive performance to have less than 100 yards. I know you're just trying to get through the game. Is that the easiest explanation or or is it concerning that they weren't able to move the ball more consistently? >> No, that was concerning. It's not an easy explanation at all. You got to get more than 100 yards and you don't want to get shut out ever regardless of who's playing in preseason. Uh we're trying to win the game. We were trying to be physical up front on both sides of the football. Uh defensively, the guys up front played well. Offensively, they didn't. >> Todd, as you're trying to make the the tough final decisions for the 53, does having injured reserve to start the season like with the intended return, does that help you at all? Are there guys that are in play for that or is that not really the case right now? >> We'll get the injury report today, but there's a few guys that might be in place for that. We don't have as many as we thought we would have, but there's probably one or two guys in place for that. >> Okay. Thank you, >> Rich Straoud. >> Think I know where this is going, but coach, have you decided uh whether whether you can keep three quarterbacks on the 53man roster if that's your plan? >> Something we got to talk about uh probably right after this. We're going to meet on it this morning and we're going to go over something that way. It's a discussion, but Not at a definite. >> And and uh what's what's the pros and cons? I mean, obviously the pros is you keep an extra quarterback, but but how difficult is it in this day and age to have that many on the active roster? >> It's difficult because you probably need a spot for somewhere else as far as teams or an extra rusher or an extra backer, an extra offensive line. And so knowing that guy's not going to play in case of emergency, I think every position would like to have insurance behind the insurance. He's been great for the room. You know, we're trying to kick off and punt because we're trying to see who can make the team. We haven't put our total unit out there together yet. We put guys out there that were battling for positions against each other, try to make them compete and make the team that way.
