Uh obviously he needs time on task at the position to get some of the rust off of that way but he played fast and he played hard on teams and you know he didn't have much action his way. He did get a tackle in there on the cut back run but other than that it's just a matter of him just getting reps and seeing everything so the health part was the biggest thing and he played a whole half so that was good to see. >> Thanks coach >> Greg Almond if any media have questions please raise your hand. [snorts] Todd, what you were talking about special teams. One job we really haven't talked about at all is long snapper. You guys have Evan Decker's back from last year. I think he was the first guy in in all three games. Uh but you did alternate him and Daly last night. Just just curious about that job and and whether that's still a competition. >> It was still a competition going into last night. Again, we'll evaluate that as we meet with Danny when he comes in and we'll kind of go from there. >> Okay. Thanks, Tom. There we go. Um, are you in a position where you can keep four running backs and and I know you're still working on the puzzle in terms of having it all pieces together where you keep three quarterbacks or not, but can you maybe shed some light on how the battle for the third string running back between Josh Williams and Shawn Tucker has gone this preseason, whether it's kickoff returns or whether it's as a runner or receiver and pass protector. >> That's a tough battle. It kind of went back and forth every game. Uh both of them can run the ball. Both of them return kicks obviously. Uh both of them try to tackle on kickoff and punt team and it's a matter of keeping four running backs, three quarterbacks. You know, there's some extra receiver involved, obviously a corner involved, a defensive lineman. So all that's going to be in the discussion, but that'll be a tough call because they're both good football players. >> Thanks, Todd. >> Last one from Rick Shrup. I think most people recognize your offensive line when it's healthy as one of the tops in the NFL. Um, how do you feel about your depth though? And I know you played a lot of guys last night, but um, just the inconsistency there uh, to run the football really even protect, you know, either quarterback >> with Chuke out with Skoolie out, you know, from a tackle standpoint, the depth is thin with with three tackles out and Tristan and Luke not playing really four tackles out inside. You got to worry about the guard. Fine is experienced and he can play both spots. But the other guys got to come on a little more. Haggard and uh Klein has really got to come on a little bit more. And it was one guy here or there last night that kind of butchered the whole thing and they just didn't play well. But overall depth when you're keeping eight or nine, we think we got decent eight depth from that standpoint, but we can't get anybody hurt. >> Gotcha. Thanks, coach. [clears throat] >> All right, that's all we have. Thanks, coach. Thanks.

title: Todd Bowles Speaks After Preseason Finale vs. Jags | Press Conference
text: Hey coach, um first your decision to uh you know, to start Jaylon and play him into the third quarter. >> Oh, we definitely want to see more of him. Want him to get some more experience. Want him to play against uh the twos and the fours and threes and fours and get them in there and see how he operated. We're going to go back and evaluate and all that. It's not really the place to discuss the overall operation. Make sure he's fine with that. And then we'll come back and look at the film and see what it is. You know, it wasn't very good offensively tonight. >> What's your reaction to the overall performance of the team tonight? >> Not good enough. Anytime you get shut out, you know, I I think we protected the quarterback, but that wasn't good. We couldn't run the ball. We got a special teams touchdown. Defense fought and had some mistakes, but I think they fought. I thought Tua had a great game. He didn't show it. >> Uh we saw Keionte Scott get a little banged up. Any update on him or what injury he has? >> Not yet. I think it's an ankle. I'm going to wait and see. >> How about Mo Kamara? Mo Kamara from what >> Uh I think it's a knee, but I'm waiting to see what it is and what they >> Now, Benjamin Morrison made a a nice play there breaking up a touchdown. Um for him to battle through his injury and then get some game reps here, how how happy are you with what you've seen out of him as he turned into the regular season? >> When I watch the tape, it's just good to see him play a half. So, he's just got to get the time on task now and get the get the reps in. >> Coach, in in a game like this guys are fighting for the last roster spots, do you think that guys like Aiden Gardens and Jack Pyburn maybe helped themselves out a little bit tonight? >> I'm going to look at the tape, obviously. Uh I know Pyburn had what, one or two sacks? He sure had two sacks again. I got to look at the totality of it at the deep position as well. Garns has been playing consistent the last few weeks. So, you know, we got some tough decisions to make. >> Seemed like there were a few special teams mishaps including that turn. What was your evaluation of the special teams play in total? >> Obviously, we gave up a touchdown. It's not very good. They made some plays in the first half. I think they got worn out a little bit playing offense and defense and playing special teams in the second half. But, you know, what it takes in this league to make this team. >> Are there any positions that you might think are the the most difficult to make a decision on with these roster cuts coming? >> They're all difficult. You know, when you get to know these guys and be around them all, it doesn't matter the position. It is hard to tell people that they're they're not going to be on the team anymore. >> Do you have any concerns about the depth of your offensive line? I know you you like your first five guys and maybe a couple swing tackles. >> I like the first five when everybody's healthy. I'll look at the tape. If you judge by tonight, yeah, there is concern over it. But, I'll look at the totality of the tape and see where it came from. >> Anything else? >> Thank you. Thank you very much. >> Thanks very much. Appreciate it. >> It's good, y'all. >> Jalen, how would you evaluate your performance tonight? >> Um a lot of miscues, a lot of things that, you know, we definitely could have done better offensively. Um obviously, you know, when you go up there and you don't score any points, that's that's nothing that you, you know, you don't really want, especially as a quarterback. And um obviously, we haven't watched the film yet, but I think I do think that there was uh some good things that we did on film as well. And um obviously, there were some things that we need to clean up. So, we're going to go go ahead, look at the film, and get better from there. >> What have you learned out from there? How about the way you tried your whole season or preseason and trying to get >> Yeah, I mean, um as I've come to you to tell y'all since since getting here, um I have God on my side. And I truly believe that, you know, everything that that I've been able to do up to this point is has been because of him. So, um I'm not going to lose faith. I'm I'm going to keep my faith in God. And at the end of the day, everything is going to happen. Everything that happens happens for a reason. And um I'm going to let God handle those decisions. >> Jalen, when did you learn that you were going to start this game and play into the third quarter? And do you feel like that was a, you know, because of what you did the first two games, an opportunity to maybe become the backup to Baker Mayfield? >> Yeah, I mean, you know, I'm I'm someone who always says whenever your number's called, you got to be able to you got to be ready to go out there and play football. Uh so, whenever they told me uh today that I was going to be able to go out there and start, I was like, all right, bet. Let's go out there and play some football. Like I've been like I keep telling y'all, I've been playing this game since I was a kid. So, being able to get those extra reps, being able to to go out there and be the first quarterback out there, obviously, that's that's a dream come true, you know, being able to start a NFL game as a starting quarterback. That's something that that you always dream of. So, obviously grateful for the opportunity. Um and you know, like I said, we got to get better from there. >> How tough was it though because the protection wasn't good? You had some dropped passes on third down. How hard was it to get things going? >> Uh obviously we never we never caught a rhythm tonight. So, um I'm always remain confident in my abilities, remain confident in being able to to run this system. And um like I keep saying, we're going to get better. >> How do you feel about your preseason as a whole? >> Um I think that there is definitely some good in there, but obviously like I keep telling y'all, I'm someone who I believe I'm my worst critic. And uh as much as people want to say that there's good in there, I always look at the bad. Look at all the miss the miss passes, the miss pre-snap checks. I mean, we had a fumble today. And um that's 100% on me. I have to be able to communicate better. And um the when you're looking at those little things, you want to be able to grow from it. >> This guy got signed after the draft. Did you get any special kick out of seeing guys like Aidan Gardner and Jack Coan >> Absolutely. Yeah, no, absolutely. I mean, um to be able to see a a UDFA go out there and make plays, that's something you love to see because, you know, they go out there with that chip on their shoulder. And I've been able to see AG be able to perform literally since rookie minicamp. Jack Pyburn has been someone who's continued to make plays day in and day out. Like he's told y'all about his work ethic and how much he does on a day-to-day basis, being one of the first guys in the building and being able to do as much as he can to prepare himself to go out there and play football. >> I know you're a confident player and I know you've been playing this game a long time, but um does does this your preseason what you've done kind of confirm to you that look, I should have been drafted. I know that that you know, all that stuff that happened you know, that that you're going to be a good player in this league. Like I keep saying, my journey's my journey. God put me in this position for a reason. And um something my mom told me at after the draft was I don't know why you're in this position, but at the end of the day it's happening to you for a reason. And I think that God gives his toughest battles to his strongest soldiers. So, if I'm in a position where I have to be able to show others that this mountain can be moved, then that's exactly what I'm going to do. I'm going to go out there and um do everything that I can to be able to go out there and make plays. So, um draft pick, UDFA, doesn't matter. I got the opportunity to be able to come out here and play NFL football. So, I'm forever grateful for that. >> Appreciate y'all. Y'all too. >> Appreciate it. Appreciate it.

What did you like about the effort there in the fourth quarter and then also >> Yeah, guys playing tremendously hard. I mean, look, these guys are playing special teams, too. Um, you know, stack. So, um but I like that I like the fact that we can throw it without having to drop back. >> What have you seen in all the practices in camp that the fans didn't see in the preseason games because the starters didn't play? What did you see from the starters all camp that says they're ready for the open? >> Well, I think our I think our operation is um is on its way. There's a lot of confidence with our ones. It means both sides are making plays and making plays. Um they've been really competitive and so uh you know you see some of the you just you don't see like a full game's worth of like how you know how we're going to operate and us handling but we're doing a ton of tremendous situation work. guys are in in lock step with each other. Um, still room plenty of room for growth. Um, whether or not our guys started this this preseason or not, there's going to be times in our in the first few games to quarter of the season where, you know, we're going to have to do a great job evaluating where we're at, what we're good at, and making decisions on on where we go. That happens every year. That happened last year. It happened our first year here. um that's just the way that the what the way life is, you know, like and where the league's going, how people are defending you, you know, what you're efficient at, things like that. So, um but that's that's a process we're going to have to navigate as a staff together and I'm confident we can do that with the people we have. >> You get the Chiefs uh back home in a couple months.
